Policy: Law No. 1845 “On the use of nuclear energy”.
Policy_Content: This Law defines legal, organizational and economic bases of public relations when in the process of use of nuclear energy and is aimed at protecting life and human health, environment, property, ensuring the regime of non-proliferation of nuclear weapons, strengthening the international security regime of the use of atomic energy, nuclear and radiation safety and safety in the use of nuclear energy. The main principles of legal regulation in the field of the use of nuclear energy are: (a) ensuring nuclear and radiation safety when using nuclear energy, protection of the population and the environment from radiation hazard; (b) availability, objectivity and timeliness of information related to the use of nuclear energy and the impact on the population and the environment, if this information does not contain information constituting a state secret; (c) return of spent nuclear fuel to the manufacturer; (d) ensuring state verification and supervision of nuclear and radiation safety and nuclear security in the process of the use of nuclear energy; (e) ensuring social protection of the personnel of nuclear facilities; and (f) compensation for damage caused by radiation exposure. The objects of use of atomic energy are: (a) nuclear installations; (b) storage facilities for nuclear and other radioactive materials, storage facilities for radioactive waste, stationary facilities and structures intended for storage or disposal of nuclear and other radioactive materials, as well as spent nuclear fuel and radioactive waste; (c) nuclear materials; (d) spent nuclear fuel; (e) radioactive waste; and (f) sources of ionizing radiation, with indicators above the withdrawal level. State regulation in the field of the use of atomic energy shall be applicable  in relation to: (a) licensing of activities related to all stages of the life cycle of the nuclear energy installation; (b) handling of nuclear and other radioactive materials, including the process of exploration and extraction of minerals containing these substances, as well as in the process of manufacturing, use, processing, transportation and storage of nuclear and other radioactive materials, spent nuclear fuel and radioactive waste; (c) conducting scientific research, performing work and providing services related to the use of nuclear energy, including research reactors; (d) physical protection of nuclear installations, storage and disposal facilities for nuclear and other radioactive materials, spent nuclear fuel and radioactive waste; (e) safety and nuclear security in the process of the use of nuclear energy; (f) accounting and control of nuclear materials, sources of ionizing radiation, spent nuclear fuel and radioactive waste; (g)  export and import of nuclear materials, technologies and equipment, special non-nuclear materials, materials, technologies and dual-use equipment, sources of ionizing radiation; (h) monitoring of the radiation situation in the territory of the Republic of Tajikistan; (i) transit transportation of nuclear materials and other radioactive materials through the territory of the Republic of Tajikistan; (j)  inspection and supervision of the activities of legal entities and individual entrepreneurs in the process of performing work related to the life cycle of nuclear facilities; (k) expertise of nuclear and radiation safety and nuclear security; and (l) training and certification of personnel employed at nuclear energy facilities. This Law consists of VII Sections divided into 35 Articles. Section I lays down general provisions. Section II regards state regulation in the field of the use of nuclear energy. Section III establishes terms and conditions for the activities related to the use of nuclear energy. Section IV regards expertise of nuclear and radiation safety and nuclear security, accreditation of organizations performing expertise of nuclear and radiation safety. Section V establishes rights and duties of natural and legal persons. Section VI establishes guarantees in the field of nuclear energy. Section VII lays down final provisions.

Policy: Regulation on maximum permissible noise levels with regard to the type of noise source, time and place of occurrence.
Policy_Content: This Regulation, based on the provisions of the Croatian Law on noise protection, prescribes the maximum permissible noise levels with regard to the type of noise source, time and place of such noise occurrence. The provisions of this text shall apply to the time period 'day', the time period 'evening' and the time period 'night' as well as to the all-day period 'day-evening-night'. The beginning, end and duration of time periods shall be determined by a special regulation governing the area of noise protection. Zone of mixed, mostly business purposes with housing, with occasional housing, mostly agricultural holdings are also included in the noise list-table (see article 4). Noise source is any machine, device, installation, plant, technological process, road traffic, railway traffic, air traffic, water traffic, as well as noise of industrial plants and plants, electroacoustic device for broadcasting music and speech. Sources of noise are also considered units as immovable and movable objects and open and closed spaces for recreation, games, dancing, plays, concerts, ect.

Policy: Decreto Nº 253 - Ley General de los recursos hídricos.
Policy_Content: La presente ley, de orden público, tiene como fin regular la gestión integral de las aguas, su sostenibilidad, garantizar el derecho humano al agua, la seguridad hídrica para una mejor calidad de vida de todos los habitantes del país; y promover el desarrollo humano, social y económico mediante la utilización sustentable de los recursos hídricos.  En particular, la ley destaca: la importancia del derecho a la salud y a la vida en conexión con el acceso al agua potable y al saneamiento, considerando la obligación del Estado de reconocer el derecho al agua y al saneamiento garantizando que todas las personas puedan disponer de agua limpia, suficiente, salubre, segura, aceptable y accesible; se destaca también en la exposición de motivos la obligación del Estado de proteger los recursos naturales, así como la diversidad e integridad del medioambiente para garantizar el desarrollo sostenible; la responsabilidad de garantizar la gestión integrada de los recursos hídricos derivada de los tratados ratificados por el Estado; el agua como bien nacional de uso público, inalienable, inembargable e imprescriptible; la necesidad de atender a las variabilidades climáticas con un impacto en la agricultura y la seguridad alimentaria del país; y el rol fundamental de las mujeres en el abastecimiento, gestión y protección del agua.

Policy_Content: El objetivo del presente Acuerdo es modificar las Reglas de Operación del Programa para el Bienestar Integral de los Pueblos Indígenas correspondiente al ejercicio fiscal 2022, a cargo del Instituto Nacional de los Pueblos Indígenas. El Programa para el Bienestar Integral de los Pueblos Indígenas (PROBIPI) del Gobierno de México, atiende a los pueblos y comunidades indígenas y afromexicanas, en su carácter de sujetos colectivos de derecho público, respetando plenamente su libre determinación y autonomía en los términos reconocidos en la legislación nacional e internacional. El Programa hace realidad la nueva relación del Estado con los pueblos y comunidades indígenas y afromexicanas, de tal forma que las acciones serán construidas a través de procesos de planeación participativa, con una visión sostenible y tomando en consideración sus legítimas demandas, reivindicaciones y aspiraciones de vida.  Los proyectos que plantea el PROBIPI buscan ser de alcance comunitario y regional, incentivan su organización como colectivo y perfilan su reconstitución como pueblos al hacer posible la participación de gobiernos comunitarios indígenas, así como la de sus instituciones representativas. La cobertura del Programa será Nacional y atenderá a pueblos y comunidades indígenas y afromexicanas ubicadas, preferentemente, en las regiones de atención focalizada prioritaria definidas por el INPI durante el ejercicio fiscal.

Policy: Law No. 434-VI “On social services”.
Policy_Content: This Law determines the legal, organizational and economic the basis for the provision of social services to certain categories of persons. Social service shall be intended a set of measures and actions taken to meet the individual needs of certain categories of persons, with the purpose of improving their living conditions and (or) expanding their opportunities to independently provide their basic individual needs, as well as to overcome a difficult life situation. User of social services shall be intended a person who is recognized as needing the provision of social services and to whom social services are provided. Social service providers shall be intended social service institutions, and also other legal entities, regardless of the form of ownership and (or) individual entrepreneurs providing social services. This Law applies to citizens of Turkmenistan, foreign citizens and stateless persons permanently residing in territory of Turkmenistan, refugees, as well as legal entities regardless of the form of ownership and individual entrepreneurs, operating in the field of social services. The goals of social services are: (a) promotion of equal opportunities for all members of society, aimed at strengthening social cohesion and preventing social isolation; (b) assistance to lead a decent, safe and creative life, equal participation in the public life of the state; (c) assistance to persons in overcoming difficult life situations, which they are unable to resolve with their own resources and available opportunities; (d) forecasting and prevention of the occurrence of difficult life situations; and (e) intensification of their own efforts of individuals and families, creating conditions for problem solving on their own. The main principles in the field of social services are: (a) ensuring equal opportunities for the use of social services; (b) targeting; (c) availability and accessibility; (c) voluntariness; (d) observance of the rights of users of social services; (e) provision of social services taking into account individual needs of users of social services; and (f) confidentiality. The state guarantees to individuals, families, groups of persons recognized as persons in need of social services, the possibility of using social services based on an assessment of individual needs for overcoming difficult life situations. Grounds for recognizing a person in need of social services are: (a) disability; (b) old age; (c) the consequences of an industrial injury and occupational disease; (d) loss of a breadwinner, loneliness, orphanhood, homelessness and neglect; (e) lack of a fixed place of residence; (f) forced change of the country of permanent residence; (g) victim of human trafficking; (h) consequences of violence or situations associated with a risk to life; (i) family trouble; and (j) other difficult life situations. Social services can be provided on temporary or permanent basis. This Law contains VI Chapters divided into 25 Articles. Chapter I lays down general provisions. Chapter II regards state regulation and control in the field of social services. Chapter III establishes state guarantees in the field of social services. Chapter IV regards the particulars of the provision of social services. Chapter V establishes rights and obligations of users of social services and employees of the providers of social services. Chapter VI lays down final provisions.

Policy: Law No. 435-VI “On the prevention and control of non-contagious diseases”.
Policy_Content: This Law determines the legal, organizational, economic and social basis for the prevention and control of non-contagious diseases. Non-contagious diseases shall be intended a group of health disorders, resulting from a combination of genetic, physiological, environmental and behavioral factors. Prevention of non-contagious diseases shall be intended a set of measures, aimed at preventing the occurrence of non-infectious diseases, elimination of risk factors for their development. This Law applies to citizens of Turkmenistan, and also, unless otherwise provided by law and international agreements of Turkmenistan, to those residing/staying in the territory Turkmenistan foreign citizens and stateless persons. The main directions of state policy in the field of prevention of non-contagious diseases and their control are: (a) creation of necessary conditions for life and health protection of patients with non-contagious diseases; (b) maintaining the necessary social level of vital activity of patients with non-contagious diseases at any age; (c) implementation of healthcare measures, prevention, early identification, treatment and ongoing checkup of individuals at high risk or the likelihood of non-contagious diseases to prevent health complications, reducing the need for inpatient treatment and expensive high-tech interventions, as well as reducing premature mortality; (d) ensuring equal access to the established range of services for healthcare, prevention, treatment and rehabilitation, palliative assistance and a set of basic, safe, affordable, effective and high-quality medicines and medical products in accordance with the legislation of Turkmenistan; (e) implementation of measures to improve the quality of medical care in order to prevent non-contagious diseases; (f) provision of primary specialized healthcare, including medical care on a free or preferential basis, in the order established by the legislation of Turkmenistan; (g) provision of patients affected by major non-contagious diseases with medicines and medical devices for free or preferential basis in the manner prescribed by law of Turkmenistan; and (h) scientific research in the field of forecasting and development of new methods of prevention, diagnosis and treatment of non-contagious diseases. This Law contains V Chapters divided into 21 Articles. Chapter I lays down general provisions. Chapter II regards state regulation and control in the field of prevention of non-contagious diseases. Chapter III establishes organizational basis in the field of prevention of non-contagious diseases. Chapter IV establishes rights and obligations of patients affected by non-contagious diseases, and social protection of medical staff. Chapter V lays down final provisions.

Policy: Constitutional Law No. ZRU-737 “On the state of emergency.”
Policy_Content: The scope of this Constitutional Law is to determine conditions and procedure for the introduction of a state of emergency throughout the territory or in certain areas of the Republic of Uzbekistan. State of emergency is temporarily introduced in accordance with the Constitution of the Republic of Uzbekistan throughout the territory and or in certain areas of the Republic of Uzbekistan, a special legal regime of the functioning of government bodies, local authorities, self-government bodies of citizens, non-governmental non-profit organizations and other organizations regardless of the organizational and legal form and form of ownership, their officials, allowing the establishment of the stipulated by this Constitutional Law of certain restrictions on the rights and freedoms of citizens of the Republic of Uzbekistan, foreign citizens and stateless persons, as well as the rights of legal entities and imposing on them additional responsibilities. The purpose of imposing a state of emergency is to eliminate circumstances that served as the basis for its introduction, ensuring security of citizens of the Republic of Uzbekistan and protection of the constitutional system and territorial integrity of the Republic of Uzbekistan. A state of emergency is introduced in exceptional cases under circumstances that are a direct threat to the life, health and safety of citizens of the Republic of Uzbekistan, the constitutional order and (or) territorial integrity of the Republic of Uzbekistan and the elimination of which is impossible without the use of emergency measures. These circumstances include: (a) real external threat, attempts to forcibly change the foundations of constitutional order and (or) territorial integrity of the Republic of Uzbekistan, riots, terrorist attacks, as well as blocking or seizing especially important and categorized objects or separate localities, preparation (creation) and activities of illegal armed groups, interethnic, interconfessional and border conflicts, accompanied by acts of violence that pose an imminent threat to life, health and safety of citizens, daily activities of state bodies, other organizations; and (b) major disasters, natural disasters, epidemics and others natural and man-made emergencies, environmental emergencies that require large-scale rescue and other urgent work. State of emergency throughout the territory or in certain localities of the Republic of Uzbekistan is introduced by the Decree of the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan. Legislative Chamber and Senate of the Parliament of the Republic Uzbekistan no later than 72 hours from the moment of receipt of the presidential decree on the introduction of a state of emergency consider the issue of approving this decree and take joint ruling. The duration of the state of emergency imposed throughout territory of the Republic of Uzbekistan, may not exceed thirty days, and if introduced in separate areas - sixty days. The state of emergency may be extended further for one term by decree of the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan, if the goals of the imposition of a state of emergency have not been achieved. The population is notified in the same order in which it was notified on the introduction of a state of emergency. Decree of the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan on the introduction of state of emergency for the duration of the state of emergency the following emergency measures may be envisaged and temporary restrictions: (a) special procedure for the sale, acquisition and distribution of food and essential household items; (b) restriction of the movement of vehicles and performance of their screening; and (c) suspension of the activities of hazardous industries and organizations that use explosives, radioactive, as well as hazardous chemical and biological substances. This Constitutional Law contains 7 Chapters divided into 38 Articles. Chapter 1 lays down general provisions. Chapter 2 establishes circumstances and the procedure for introduction of a state of emergency. Chapter 3 regards emergency measures and temporary restrictions applicable under conditions of emergency. Chapter 4 regards special bodies of state government set up for the period of a state of emergency. Chapter 5 regards forces and means ensuring (keeping) regime of a state of emergency. Chapter 6 establishes guarantees of the rights of natural and legal persons, and also officials under conditions of a state of emergency. Chapter 7 lays down final provisions.

Policy: Order No. 2501 on pharmacies' production of cannabis end products.
Policy_Content: The present Order, adopted by the Ministry of Health, lays down rules on pharmacies' production of cannabis end products, as defined in Article 3 of Act No. 1668 on a pilot scheme for medicinal cannabis. Only pharmacies and pharmacy branches are authorized to produce cannabis end products. The Order prohibits the production of such products by pharmacy outlets. Policy_Content: This Act provides for the prevention of hoarding in respect of scheduled articles, in the wake of an emergent situation resulting from the outbreak of the Corona virus pandemic (Covid-19). The Act describes the offence of hoarding for any dealer who is found to storing or stocking anything in excess of the maximum quantity of scheduled articles allowed to be held in stock. Policy: Resolution No. 1342 of the Cabinet of Ministers validating the Procedure for providing state support for insurance of agricultural products.
Policy_Content: The Procedure for providing state support for insurance of agricultural products defines the conditions for providing state support for insurance of agricultural commodities and the mechanism for using funds provided by the Ministry of Agriculture in the state budget under the program "Financial Support for Agricultural Commodity Producers" for state support for insurance of agricultural commodities. The main administrator of budget funds and the responsible executor of the budget program is the Ministry of Agrarian Policy. State support for insurance of agricultural products is carried out by reimbursing policyholders for part of the paid insurance payments (premiums) under the insurance contract. The recipients of budget funds are agricultural producers. State support is provided to agricultural producers - legal entities, regardless of the organizational and legal form and form of ownership, and to natural persons – entrepreneurs (policyholders): (a) in respect of which no bankruptcy cases have been initiated, which have not been declared bankrupt, that are not at the stage of liquidation; (b) who do not have, as of the first day of the month in which the decision on payments will be made, more than six months overdue payment arrears, the control of which is entrusted to the State Tax Collection Service; (c) which are not classified as legal entities or individuals to whom special economic and other restrictive measures (sanctions) are applied, according to the relevant decisions of the National Security and Defense Council of Ukraine, put into effect by the Decree of the President of Ukraine on the application of personal special economic and other restrictive measures (sanctions) in accordance with the Law of Ukraine "On Sanctions"; (d) who concluded an agricultural commodities insurance contract with state support with an insurer that has the right to insure agricultural commodities with state support (authorized insurer); and (e) who paid the insurance payment to the authorized insurer (insurance premium) under the insurance contract.

Policy: Regional Law No. 4604-KZ “On regulation of forest relations.”
Policy_Content: This Regional Law, in accordance with the Forest Code of the Russian Federation, determines the procedure and standards for the procurement of timber by citizens for their own personal needs, the procedure for harvesting and collecting non-timber forest resources by citizens, the procedure for the procurement by citizens of food forest resources and collection of medicinal plants for their own needs, as well as exceptional cases of timber extraction and procurement of non-timber forest resources on the basis of purchase and sale contracts of forest plantations on the regional territory. Citizens harvest timber for their own needs on the basis of purchase and sale contracts related to forest plantations without allotment of forest plots thereto. Timber extracted by citizens for their own needs cannot be alienated or transferred from one person to another in other ways. Timber obtained in the process of forest management and in the process of the performance of measures for their guardianship, protection, reproduction, is subject to accounting before its transportation from the forest. Citizens have the right to carry out, as a matter of priority, procurement of timber for their own needs in forest areas where is under way liquidation of the consequences of the emergency situation in the forests, which arose as a result of forest fires. The procedure for concluding a contract for the sale of forest plantations for personal needs of citizens on public forest plots shall be approved by the regional state executive authority, carrying out within the established competence management in the field of use, guardianship, protection and reproduction of forests. Procurement of timber for personal needs of citizens in public forests includes work on felling forest plantations, cutting of branches, crosscutting of timber, log hauling, stacking wood in piles, collecting windbreak and windblow in heaps for measuring, loading and removing timber from the forest, cleaning the territory of felling sites in accordance with the requirements of forest legislation. This Regional Law establishes the amount of timber authorized for procurement by citizens for individual personal needs.

Policy: Executive Order on Catalyzing Clean Energy Industries and Jobs Through Federal Sustainability.
Policy_Content: The Order recognizes that the Federal Government faces broad exposure to the mounting risks and costs already posed by the climate crisis. In responding to this crisis, U.S. has a once-in-a-generation economic opportunity to create and sustain jobs, including well-paying union jobs; support a just transition to a more sustainable economy for American workers; strengthen America’s communities; protect public health; and advance environmental justice. The Federal Government can catalyze private sector investment and expand the economy and American industry by transforming electricity, vehicles, buildings, and other operations to be clean and sustainable. The policy therefore aims to lead a carbon pollution-free electricity sector by 2035 and net-zero emissions economy-wide by no later than 2050.

Policy_Content: regulates the framework for promoting the use of renewable energy in a sustainable manner, regulates the planning and encouragement of the production and consumption of electricity produced in production facilities that use renewable energy sources and high-efficiency cogeneration, determines the measures of encouragement for the production of electricity using renewable sources energy and high-efficiency cogeneration, the implementation of the system for encouraging the production of electricity from renewable energy sources and high-efficiency cogeneration, as well as financial support for electricity produced from renewable energy sources and high-efficiency cogeneration for own needs, is regulated, rules on administrative procedures and information and training are prescribed through new educational programs and retraining programs, regulates the maintenance of the register of renewable energy sources and high-efficiency cogeneration for projects, project holders and privileged producers of electricity from renewable energy sources and high-efficiency cogeneration, regulates the issue of the guarantee of origin of renewable energy, regulates the issue of international cooperation in the field of renewable energy sources, as well as criteria for sustainability reduction of greenhouse gas emissions, and regulates other issues of importance for the use of renewable energy sources and high-efficiency cogeneration. This Law also regulates the acquisition of the status of privileged energy producer for production plants that use any of the primary forms of renewable energy sources in the Republic of Croatia and/or high-efficiency cogeneration. The use of renewable energy sources and high-efficiency cogeneration is of interest to the Republic of Croatia. The purpose of this Law is to promote the production of electricity and heat from renewable energy sources and high-efficiency cogeneration, to promote the production of electricity and heat from renewable energy sources and high-efficiency cogeneration at the point of consumption, to increase the shares in the total final consumption of energy produced from renewable energy sources by using incentive mechanisms and the regulatory framework for the use of renewable energy sources and high-efficiency cogeneration, and to fulfill the goals of the Republic of Croatia and contribute to the goals of the European Union in accordance with the international obligations of the European Union for decarbonization. This Law incorporates into Croatian legislation certain thematic EU legislative documents (as specified in article 3).

Policy: Ordinance on Measures for the Control of Almond Grass (Almond Grass Ordinance).
Policy_Content: This Ordinance regulates the measures to be taken for the control of the common almond grass in particular (a) the detection of an infestation; b) the control of an infestation on cultivated land; c) the measures to prevent its spread; and d) the promotion and compensation measures. The Ordinance provides for the monitoring obligations to determine an infestation, review and mapping of the infested area by the Office for the Environment, and to take control measures and to combat. The Ordinance further provides for the actions to be taken for excavation, keeping the area free of vegetation and management adjustment in the infested area, laying out buffer strip, cleaning of tillage equipment and machines and disposal of excavated plant materials and soil. Policy: Decree No. 124 of the Ministry of Public Health validating the Regulation on the sectoral subsystem of the State System for Prevention and Elimination of Emergencies.
Policy_Content: This Regulation defines the main tasks, functions, structure, composition of forces and means, the procedure for the functioning of the sectoral subsystem of the State emergency prevention and liquidation systems of the Ministry of Public Health. Sanitary and epidemiological intelligence shall be intended timely and continuous receipt of reliable information on sanitary and epidemiological situation in the emergency zone related to natural and man-made disasters. Sectoral subsystem of the State System for Prevention and Elimination of Emergencies shall be integral part of the state early warning system and is intended for organization and implementation of work to protect state organizations subordinated to the Ministry and public health from emergency situations, prevention and elimination of medical and sanitary consequences of emergencies and disasters. The main tasks of sectoral subsystem shall be as follows: (a) provision of medical care to the population affected by emergencies; (b) collection, compilation, analysis and presentation of emergency data to authorities about victims in emergency zones; (c) constant monitoring of changes in the sanitary and epidemiological situation at the national level; (d) forecasting and assessment of risk in emergency zones; and (e) forecasting and assessment of health consequences in emergencies.

Policy: Regulation (EU) 2021/2115 establishing rules on support for strategic plans to be drawn up by Member States under the common agricultural policy (CAP Strategic Plans) and financed by the European Agricultural Guarantee Fund (EAGF) and by the European Agricultural Fund for Rural Development (EAFRD) and repealing Regulations (EU) No 1305/2013 and (EU) No 1307/2013.
Policy_Content: This Regulation lays down rules on support for CAP strategic plans to be drawn up by Member States and financed by the EAGF and the EAFRD, with the aim of making the Common Agricultural Policy more result-driven and market-oriented, boosting modernization and sustainability, including the economic, social, environmental and climate sustainability of the agricultural, forestry and rural areas, and helping reduce the Union legislation-related administrative burden for beneficiaries. Each CAP Strategic Plan shall cover the period from 1 January 2023 to 31 December 2027. This Regulation sets out general as well as specific objectives for agricultural and rural development, including (i) supporting viable farm income and resilience of the agricultural sector across the Union in order to enhance long-term food security and agricultural diversity as well as ensuring the economic sustainability of agricultural production in the Union;  (ii) enhancing market orientation and increasing farm competitiveness both in the short and long term, including greater focus on research, technology and digitalization; (iii) improving the farmers’ position in the value chain; (iv) contributing to climate change mitigation and adaptation, including by reducing greenhouse gas emissions and enhancing carbon sequestration, as well as promoting sustainable energy; (v) fostering sustainable development and efficient management of natural resources such as water, soil and air, including by reducing chemical dependency; (vi) contributing to halting and reversing biodiversity loss, enhance ecosystem services and preserve habitats and landscapes; (vii) attracting and sustaining young farmers and new farmers and facilitating sustainable business development in rural areas; (viii) promoting employment, growth, gender equality, including the participation of women in farming, social inclusion and local development in rural areas, including the circular bio-economy and sustainable forestry; (ix) improving the response of Union agriculture to societal demands on food and health, including high-quality, safe and nutritious food produced in a sustainable way, to reduce food waste, as well as to improve animal welfare and to combat antimicrobial resistance. These objectives shall be complemented and interconnected with the cross-cutting objective of modernizing agriculture and rural areas by fostering and sharing of knowledge, innovation and digitalization in agriculture and rural areas and by encouraging their uptake by farmers, through improved access to research, innovation, knowledge exchange and training. Member States shall include in their CAP Strategic Plans a system of conditionality under which farmers and other beneficiaries receiving direct payments or annual payments are subject to an administrative penalty if they do not comply with the statutory management requirements under Union law and the GAEC standards relating to the climate and the environment, including water, soil and biodiversity of ecosystems; public health and plant health; and animal welfare. This Regulation lays down rules on the definitions and conditions to be provided in the CAP Strategic Plans; common requirements and conditionality; farm advisory services; types of intervention, reduction and minimum requirements; general requirements for receiving decoupled direct payments; complementary income support; schemes for the climate, the environment and animal welfare; granting of payment; types of intervention in the fruit and vegetables sector, the apiculture products sector, the wine sector, the hops sector, the olive oil and table olives sector, and other sectors covering products listed in Annex VI to this Regulation; types of intervention for rural development; granting of support for investments, including investments in irrigation in new and existing irrigated areas; granting support for the setting-up of young farmers and the start-up of rural businesses; granting support for risk management tools; granting support for knowledge exchange and dissemination of information; specific rules for financial instruments; forms of grants; financial provisions; content of the CAP Strategic Plan; approval and amendment of the CAP Strategic Plan; and monitoring, reporting and evaluation.

Policy: Balochistan Public Private Partnership Act, 2021 (Act No. XXV of 2021).
Policy_Content: The Act provides on the establishment of the Public Private Partnership (PPP) Board and institutional arrangement that shall be constituted to promote, approve and supervise PPP projects in the Province.  The Act further elaborates on the functions of the PPP Board and establishment of the PPP Unit and Authority and allocation of PPP Authority fund. The PPP Authority is responsible for initiating, developing, and executing PPP Agreements with concessionaires, following a structured process that involves project identification, prioritization based on value for money, technical, financial, and socio-economic viability over the expected duration of the project, environmental impact assessment analysis, risk assessment and approval by the Executive Committee or PPP Board. PPP Agreements shall include among others environmental and safety requirements. The Government may provide support for PPP projects through administrative assistance in obtaining necessary licenses and clearances, facilitating utility connections, land acquisition, rehabilitation efforts, and leasing or licensing of government-owned assets. Additionally, in certain cases, the Government may offer equity in the form of land or infrastructure facilities, evaluated based on market value or projected future cash flows, subject to approval by the PPP Board as outlined in the PPP Rules.

Policy: Loi transposant la directive (UE) 2019/633 du Parlement européen et du Conseil du 17 avril 2019 sur les pratiques commerciales déloyales dans les relations interentreprises au sein de la chaîne d’approvisionnement agricole et alimentaire et modifiant le Code de droit économique.
Policy_Content: La présente loi transpose la directive (UE) 2019/633 du Parlement européen et du Conseil du 17 avril 2019 sur les pratiques commerciales déloyales dans les relations interentreprises au sein de la chaîne d'approvisionnement agricole et alimentaire. La transposition comporte des modifications du Code de droit économique. En particulier, certaines définitions contenues dans le livre I, titre 2, chapitre 4, sont modifiées (produits agricoles et alimentaires, acheteur, autorité publique, fournisseur. En suite, dans le livre VI, titre 4, chapitre 2, du même Code, il est inséré une section 4 intitulée: “Section 4. Pratiques du marché déloyales dans les relations interentreprises au sein de la chaîne d'approvisionnement agricole et alimentaire. Dans la section 4, il est insérée par l'article 4, un article VI.109/4 sur l'application du titre 3/1 du présent livre et des sections 1 à 3 du présent chapitre. Également, dans cette même section 4, il est inséré un article VI.109/5 concernant les pratiques du marché déloyales et interdites. Aussi, dans la même section 4, il est inséré un article VI.109/6 sur les pratiques du marché qui sont présumées déloyales, à moins qu'elles n'aient été préalablement convenues en termes clairs et dépourvus d'ambiguïté dans l'accord de fourniture ou dans tout accord ultérieur entre le fournisseur et l’acheteur. Encore, dans la même section 4, il est inséré un article VI.109/7 sur les mesures que le Roi peut adopter en vue d'assurer la loyauté des relations commerciales les entre les acteurs de la chaîne d'approvisionnement agricole et alimentaire.Finalement, dans la même section 4, il est inséré un article VI.109/8 sur l'interdiction des pratiques du marché déloyales entre un acheteur et un fournisseur et la nullité des clauses contractuelles qui ont pour objet des pratiques du marchés déloyales entre un acheteur et un fournisseur. La transposition de la Directive comporte aussi des modifications du livre XV du Code de droit économique: il est inséré un article XV.16/3, dans le livre XV, titre 1er, chapitre 2, section 1re, sur la presentation des plaintes, de la part d'un plaignant de la chaîne d'approvisionnement agricole et alimentaire,lorsqu’il existe des raisons de soupçonner l'existence d'infractions aux dispositions.Dans la même section 1re, il est inséré un article XV.16/4, sur les actions prévues lorsqu'une infraction est constatée.Dans la même section 1re, il est inséré un article XV.16/5, sur la coopération entre les agents visés par la loi et ceux désignées des autres États membres afin de se prêter mutuellement assistance lors de l'exécution d'enquêtes ayant une dimension transfrontalière. Le Chapitre 7, sur la possibilité de rendre publique une décision infligeant une amende administrative, est aussi modifié.

Policy: Order No. 382 of the Ministry of Agrarian Policy validating the Rules on ensuring soil fertility and the use of certain agrochemicals.
Policy_Content: The Rules on ensuring soil fertility and the use of certain agrochemicals are established for the purpose of protecting waters and soils, reducing the risk of their contamination with nitrogen compounds from agricultural sources, as a result of the use of nitrogen fertilizers. The use of nitrogen fertilizers for the cultivation of agricultural crops should be aimed at minimizing and avoiding the possibility of leaching of nitrogen compounds and pollution of waterbodies thereby. Potential losses of nitrogen compounds into the natural environment and the efficiency of their use by plants depend on a number of factors and conditions, the changes of which should be accompanied by the adjustment of fertilizer rates or doses in relation to: (a) soil and climate zones; (b) hydro-geological conditions of the territory; (c) agricultural techniques used in the economy; (d) type of agricultural crops grown; (e) the type and forms of nitrogen fertilizers used; and (f) terms and methods of applying fertilizers. The conduct of agricultural activities and the use of agricultural land should be carried out with the consideration of the need for: (a) observance of the regime of the territories and objects of the nature reserve fund, their protection zones and lands reserved for protected areas; (b) ensuring the preservation of bio- and landscape diversity, including natural habitats and species of wild fauna and flora in the territories of the Emerald network (Areas of Special Conservation Interest, ASCI), promoting the formation of an eco-network, also by preserving ecologically stabilizing lands (hayfields, pastures, protective plantations, etc.) and increasing their share in the structure of land use; (c) adaptation to climate change and its mitigation; (d) preventing the degradation of land and other natural resources, ensuring their sustainable use, promoting the restoration of meadow, steppe, wetland and other anthropogenically altered valuable ecosystems. To ensure sustainable land use, crop rotation, their optimal ratio and maintenance of soil quality, land management projects should be developed in accordance with current legislation.

Policy_Content: This Order approves the Regulation of the System of Incentives for Companies dealing with «Promotion of the Sustainable Bioeconomy», arising from the PRR allocation, which affects the investment TC-C12-i01 Bioeconomy. The economic and social crisis caused by the COVID-19 disease pandemic led to the adoption of a set of exceptional measures by the European Union (EU) and its Member States. In order to quickly respond to the main needs related to the recovery of EU countries, the European Council defined an expressive financial package aimed at supporting Member States in overcoming the socio-economic effects of the pandemic and in implementing effective recovery and recovery policies. promoting the resilience of national economies in a logic of sustainability. This Regulation, consisting of 21 articles and one Annex, creates the incentive system for companies "Promotion of Sustainable Bioeconomy", and aims to accelerate the production of high added value products originating from biological resources as an alternative to fossil-based materials. The "Promotion of Sustainable Bioeconomy" business incentives system is financed by the PRR, in compliance with the rules defined in Regulation (EU) 2021/241 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 12 February 2021, which creates the Recovery Mechanism and Resilience, in Regulation (EU) No. 651/2014 of the European Commission, and by the technical guidelines approved by the Mission Structure “Recover Portugal” (EMRP). The Incentive System for the Promotion of the Sustainable Bioeconomy applies to all economic activities that contribute to Integrated Projects in the following areas: a) Textile and clothing sector; b) Footwear sector; c) Natural resin.

Policy: Order No. 749 of the Ministry of Environmental Protection and Natural Resources validating Forest Management Procedure.
Policy_Content: Forest Management Procedure defines a unified system and conditions for organizing and carrying out forest management. Forest management is carried out by state forest management organizations. The object of forest management shall be forest plots and non-forested land plots, which are provided for use or ownership in accordance with the established procedure and are used for the needs of forestry, including field protection forest strips located on agricultural land, provided for permanent use by state or communal specialized enterprises or for rent to natural persons and legal entities. Technical documentation on forest management consists of instructive methodical materials regulating procedures, protocols, methods of collecting, processing and transmitting information about indicators, control of works, other technical aspects of field and chamber work. Technical documentation is drawn up and approved by the forest management organization. Forest management materials are updated on the basis of annual forest assessment works and/or information about changes received from the forest user. During forest management, the following shall be carried out: (a) identification of stands in need of felling in order to improve the qualitative composition of forests; (b) determination of the scope of works related to forest restoration and afforestation, protection of forests against fires, protection from pests and diseases, other forestry protection measures; and (c) design of forestry activities, procedure and methods of their implementation.

Policy: Law No. ZRU-728 “On privatization of non-agricultural land.”
Policy_Content: The scope of this Law is to regulate relations in the field of privatization of land plots of non-agricultural destination. Privatization of a land plot shall be intended alienation of non-agricultural land pertaining to state ownership, and transfer thereof in the ownership of citizens and (or) legal entities of the Republic of Uzbekistan. The main principles of land privatization are: legality; voluntariness; compensation; integrity of privatized land plots and located real estate objects on them; and openness and transparency. Objects of privatization are: (a) land provided for entrepreneurial activities and urban land-use planning to legal entities; (b) land plots provided to citizens of the Republic Uzbekistan for individual housing construction and maintenance of a residential building, as well as the implementation of entrepreneurial and urban land-use planning activities; (c) land plots on which are located objects of state-owned real estate subject to privatization; and (d) free land. Privatization of land plots is carried out in the following forms: (a) redemption by subjects of privatization of land plots allotted thereto with the right of permanent use (possession), lease or lifetime inheritable possession; and (b) purchase of land plots through an electronic online auction. This Law contains 6 Chapters divided into 44 Articles. Chapter 1 lays down general provisions. Chapter 2 regards state management in the field of privatization of land plots. Chapter 3 regards privatization of land plots pertaining to the subjects of privatization on the rights of permanent use (ownership), lease or lifelong inheritable possession. Chapter 4 regards privatization of land plots through electronic online auction. Chapter 5 establishes legal status of privatized land plots. Chapter 6 lays down final provisions.

Policy: Governmental Decision No. 1848-N validating the Regulation on reclamation works for biological rehabilitation of land disturbed by subsoil management after the closure of subsoil management facilities.
Policy_Content: This Regulation establishes the procedure for the performance of reclamation works for biological rehabilitation of land disturbed by subsoil management after the closure of subsoil management facilities. It shall be applicable to exploration, geological study of mineral deposits, mining and extraction of minerals, management of subsoil waste, and technical and biological reclamation (rehabilitation) of waste from closed subsoil management facilities. Reclamation works are carried out in two stages: technical and biological. The technical stage of reclamation of disturbed land includes measures to prepare the surface for the implementation of the biological stage, taking into account the application of land reclamation for further use according to the intended purpose. The technical phase envisages the implementation of complex works aimed at eliminating the sources of negative impact on the soil, including landslides, planning, sloping, extraction of soil and possible fertile rocks, relocation and their placement on reclaimed land. Implementation of construction of hydraulic structures. Measures shall be taken during the removal, transfer and storage of the fertile soil layer, which exclude the deterioration of the soil quality, as well as prevention of the erosion of fertile soil layer by sowing grass and strengthening the surface of the landfill by other means. The biological stage of rehabilitation of disturbed land is a set of agrochemical-phytomeliorative measures aimed at restoring the fertility, biological efficiency, ecological diversity of the ecosystem.  The biological stage of reclamation is the final process of restoration of disturbed land. Reclamation shall be classified as agricultural, ecological, afforestation or recreational.

Policy: Environment Act 2021 (Chapter 30).
Policy_Content: The Environment Act 2021 ("the Act") is organised in 8 Parts and 21 Schedules. Part 1 provides a legal framework for environmental governance; it sets out a discipline for improving the natural environment and establishes the Office for Environmental Protection (OEP), a new, statutory and independent environmental body, having as its principal objective to contribute to environmental protection and the improvement of the natural environment, with functions of scrutiny, advice and enforcement. Part 1 regulates environmental targets (sections 1-7), for instance it allows the Secretary of State to set, by regulations, long-term targets in respect of any matter which relates to the natural environment, or people’s enjoyment of the natural environment; it specifies that this power must be exercised in respect of at least one matter within each priority area (air quality; water; biodiversity; resource efficiency and waste reduction) and requires the government to meet long-term targets, and to prepare remedial plans where long-term targets are not met. It also requires the government to set and meet an air quality target for fine particulate matter in ambient air and a target relating to the abundance of species. It also establishes the process by which a long-term target is set and amended.  Moreover Part 1 requires the government to have, and maintain, an Environmental Improvement Plan (sections 8-15), a plan to significantly improve the natural environment, which sets out the steps the government intends to take to improve the natural environment and the interim targets towards meeting the long-term targets. The Part continues providing powers to the Secretary of the State to exercise environmental monitoring functions (section 16); requiring the Secretary of the State to prepare a “policy statement on environmental principles” explaining how the environmental principles specified under the Act are to be interpreted and proportionately applied by Ministers of the Crown when making policy (sections 17-19); requiring the government to publish a report on the impact of all new environmental primary legislation (section 20); and requiring the government to undertake a report  on developments in “International environmental protection legislation” intended as legislation of countries and territories outside the United Kingdom, and international organisations, that is mainly concerned with environmental protection.

Policy: Regional Law No. 31-OZ “On environmental education, awareness and the formation of environmental culture.”
Policy_Content: The main goals of environmental education, awareness and formation of environmental culture are: (a) raising the level of environmental culture, environmental awareness and environmental culture of the regional population, including the improvement of knowledge in the field of environmental protection and environmental security; (b) ensuring sustainable socio-economic development of the region, timely identification and elimination of the causes of anthropogenic environmental impact; (c) formation of a careful attitude to nature; and (d) conservation of biological and landscape diversity. The main tasks of environmental education, environmental awareness and formation of environmental culture are: (a) creation of a system of environmental education and formation of environmental culture; (b) involvement of children and youth in activities aimed at environmental protection, rational use of natural resources; (c) increasing the role of protected natural areas of regional significance as environmental education centers; (d) information support of the population of the region in the field of nature management, environmental protection and environmental security; (e) involvement of citizens, public associations and non-profit organizations in participation in environmental activities; (f) formation of a responsible attitude towards separate collection of solid municipal waste; and (g) training, retraining and advanced training of specialists in the field of nature management, environmental protection and environmental security. The main principles of the organization of environmental education and formation of environmental culture are: (a) consistency, continuity and complexity of environmental education and orientation to age and social groups of the population; (b) the focus of environmental education on sustainable socio-economic development of the region and the solution of practical problems to improve the quality of the environment; (c) openness and availability of information about the state of the environment; and (d) unity of ecological educational, cultural and information space, the development of relationships between organizations in the field of environmental education and formation of environmental culture.

Policy: Law No. 1865-IX “On Fund for partial guarantees of credits in agriculture.”

The Fund does not belong to the category of state trust funds, acquires the status of a financial institution and the right to provide financial services after its inclusion in the State Register of Financial Institutions, which is maintained by the National Bank of Ukraine, and obtaining a license in accordance with the procedure established by law and regulatory legal acts National Bank of Ukraine. Participants of the Fund, in addition to the state, can be international financial organizations and other legal entities. The Fund can be a recipient of budget funds. The participants of the Fund have the right: (a) to participate in the management of the Fund in the manner prescribed by this Law; (b) receive information about the financial and economic activities of the Fund; (c) participate in the distribution of the net profit obtained as a result of the financial and economic activity of the Fund; (d) cede one's share or part of it in the authorized capital of the Fund in accordance with Article 3 of this Law; (e) to receive, in the event of liquidation of the Fund, part of the property remaining after settlements with creditors, or its value; and (f) other rights provided for by this Law and the Fund's Statute. Fund participants are obliged to: (a) implement the decisions of the General Meeting of Fund participants and the Fund Council; and (b) perform the duties established by this Law and the Foundation's Statute.

Policy: Decree on the content and method of creating a plan for protection and rescue from natural disasters and other disasters.
Policy_Content: This Decree, based on the provisions of the Law on rescue and protection in emergency situations of the Republika Srpska, sets the content and method of creating plans for protection and rescue from natural disasters and other disasters. The protection and rescue plan against natural disasters and other accidents consists of the following documents: 1) Assessment of vulnerability to natural disasters and other disasters; 2) Plan of preventive action; 3) Preparedness plan; 4) Mobilization plan; 5) Emergency action plan. The methodological approach on the basis of which the Protection and Rescue Plan is drawn up is risk-based dimensioning. Risk-based dimensioning is a process consisting of five related and interdependent phases, which enables the adaptation of protection and rescue units and teams, i.e. civil protection, rescue and emergency services and other subjects of importance for protection and rescue, their capacities, legislation, planning and other documents to existing risks. An overview of the phases of risk-based sizing can be found in Annex 1 of this text.

Policy: Loi n° 2021-016 portant refonte de la Loi n°2006-031 du 24 novembre 2006 fixant le régime juridique de la propriété foncière privée non titrée.
Policy_Content: La présente loi a pour objet de fixer les nouveaux régimes juridiques applicables aux propriétés foncières privées non titrées. En application de l’article 33 de la Loi n° 2005-019 du 17 octobre 2005 fixant les principes régissant les statuts des terres, est propriété foncière privée non titrée au sens de la présente loi l’ensemble des terrains urbains comme ruraux : - faisant l’objet d’une occupation au moins 15 années avant la promulgation de la présente loi, mais qui ne sont pas encore immatriculés ni cadastré au registre foncier ; - ne faisant partie ni du domaine public ni du domaine privé de l’Etat ou d’une Collectivité Décentralisée ou d’une personne morale du droit public ; - non situés sur une zone soumise à un statut particulier ; - appropriés selon les coutumes et les usages du lieu et du moment, appropriation, ainsi qu’aux anciennes zones de pas géométriques lesquels demeurent rattachés au domaine privé de l’Etat. -La gestion de la propriété foncière privée non titrée est de  la compétence de la Commune. A cet effet, celle –ci institue en son sein un service administratif spécifique appelé « Guichet Foncier » dont les modalités de fonctionnement sont fixés par Décret.   La création et l’ouverture d’un Guichet Foncier sont effectuées par un Arrêté pris par le Chef de l’exécutif de la Commune. A peine de nullité, aucune procédure de reconnaissance de droits d’occupation ne peut être engagée par le Guichet Foncier avant la mise en place d’un Plan Local d’Occupation Foncière par la Collectivité concernée, lequel est validé par le service topographique territorialement compétent.

Policy: Decree No. 10.845 providing for the Interministerial Committee on Climate Change and Green Growth.
Policy_Content: This Decree, consisting of 21 articles, creates the Interministerial Committee on Climate Change and Green Growth (CIMV), aiming to establish guidelines, articulate and coordinate the implementation of the country's public actions and policies related to climate change. It establishes composition, duties and responsibilities of CIMV, entitled to perform the following actions dealing with climate change and green growth: I - define the guidelines for the Brazilian Government's action in policies related to climate change; II - coordinate and guide the policies of federal agencies that have an impact, directly or indirectly, on national emissions and absorptions of greenhouse gases; III - deliberate on the Country's strategies for the elaboration, implementation, financing, monitoring, evaluation and updating of policies, plans and actions related to climate change, among which the successive Nationally Determined Contributions - NDC from Brazil, within the scope of the Paris Agreement, promulgated by Decree No. 9.073, of 5 June 2017, and its updates; IV - monitor the implementation of the NDC presented by the country in the context of the Paris Agreement, and activities of transparency and provision of information, in compliance with the decisions of the UNFCCC; V - propose updates to the National Policy on Climate Change - PNMC; VI - establish guidelines and prepare proposals for economic and financial mechanisms to be adopted to enable the implementation of the strategies that are part of the policies related to climate change, with the purpose of promoting the efficiency and effectiveness of the application of resources and maximizing the benefits and results of the policy; VII - promote coherence between the PNMC and the actions, measures and policies that have an impact, directly or indirectly, on national emissions and absorptions of greenhouse gases and on the country's ability to adapt to the effects of climate change; VIII - disseminate policies, plans and actions related to climate change, including the successive NDCs of Brazil in Brazilian society; IX - establish the specific guidelines of the National Green Growth Program, established by Decree No. 10.846 of 25 October 2021, in addition to the elaboration and governance of the actions necessary for its implementation; and X - edit complementary rules for detailing, implementation and monitoring of actions carried out within the scope of the National Green Growth Program.

Policy: Governmental Decree No. 441 validating the Regulation on State Energy Supervision Service.
Policy_Content: State Energy Supervision Service is the state executive body responsible for state energy supervision in the Republic of Tajikistan. The Service performs the following tasks in the field pertaining to its competence: (a) control over the implementation of organizational and technical measures for efficient and economical use of fuel and energy resources; (b) control over the reduction of technological consumption of electrical energy, losses of energy in the process of generation, processing, storage, transportation, distribution, trade, use or consumption; (c) control over the uninterrupted supply to consumers of electrical energy, heat and gas from suppliers of electricity, heat and gas; (d) control over compliance with the requirements of regulatory and technical documents on the quality of energy, heat and gas; (e) control over the technical and safe operation of the main structures, power plants and networks, boiler houses and heat networks of energy supply organizations, equipment and installations of consumers of electrical and thermal energy; (f) overseeing the approval and compliance with agreed standards of technological consumption of fuel and energy resources per unit of manufactured products (works, services, etc.); (g) supervision of compliance with contractual capacity indicators of connected electrical equipment and installations and electrical energy, used by consumers; (h) control over the correct application of tariffs, determination of the quantity of electrical, thermal energy and gas from the supplying organizations in settlements with consumers; (i) supervision over the organization of accounting for the production and consumption of fuel and energy resources; (j) ensuring the optimal level of reactive power compensation in electrical equipment and installations of consumers, the correctness of application of discounts and surcharges to the tariff for electric energy for reactive power compensation; (k) supervising the timely completion of knowledge testing of personnel serving power stations, networks of electrical w thermal equipment and installations according to the rules of technical operation and safety precautions; (l) issuance of permits to connect to the networks of newly installed, restored and reconstructed installations and structures of consumers of fuel and energy resources, including in-house electrical, heat and gas networks and equipment of multi-storey buildings; (m) supervision of the implementation of the plan of organizational and technical measures for the preparation of energy facilities for the autumn-winter, thunderstorm and flood downpours period; (n)  supervising the preparation for operation of seasonal facilities, including electrical equipment and installations of pumping stations, cotton-cleaning enterprises and other organizations that have a seasonal type of activity; (o) supervising the conduct of energy audits and drafting energy certificates; and (p) supervision over the correctness of the establishment and implementation of quality standards and condensate return.

Policy: Governmental Decree No. 440 validating the Regulation on National Evaluation Standards.
Policy_Content: National Evaluation Standards establish the provisions and basic principles of evaluation, requirements for the assessment of the value of immovable property, movable property, intellectual property, as well as the requirements for a report on the evaluation used in the evaluation report. The provisions of these Standards are mandatory for the performance of assessment activities on the territory of the Republic of Tajikistan. These Standards do not apply to the evaluation of historical and cultural heritage, determining the cadastral value for tax purposes and determination of the cost of privatized state property. The evaluation includes the following requirements: (a) conclusion of a contract for the evaluation; (b) identification of the object of evaluation; (c) collection and analysis of information necessary for the assessment; (d) substantiation of applied approaches to evaluation, including the choice of types of evaluation of objects of evaluation and their implementation; (e)  harmonization (generalization) of the results of applying approaches to the assessment and determination of the final value of the object of evaluation; and (f) preparation of the evaluation report. In the process of carrying out evaluation work, it is necessary to collect and analyze technical, market, accounting, financial and other information sufficient to obtain a reasonable opinion on the value of the object of evaluation. For every type of information should be indicated the source of its receipt. The customer is responsible for the completeness, accuracy of documents and other information provided to the evaluator in the process of evaluation in accordance with contract concluded between them in accordance with the legislation of the Republic of Tajikistan. The evaluator may rely on data from the fields outside the scope of its professional competence, with the involvement of specialists from other professions and the information they received. The evaluator is not entitled to use data relating to his professional competence, the reliability of which he doubts. This requirement applies in particular to data received from the customer, ordering the evaluation work, even if the customer declares its reliability. Immovable property subject to evaluation includes perennial plantations and the right to use a land plot.

Policy: Order No. 687 of the Environmental Protection and Natural Resources validating the Instructions on the preparation by employees of the State Protection Service of the Nature Reserve Fund of Ukraine of materials on administrative offences.
Policy_Content: This Instruction establishes the procedure for the preparation by employees of the State Protection Service of the Nature Reserve Fund of Ukraine of materials on administrative offences. If the offence is committed by several persons, the protocol on the administrative offence is drawn up for each person separately. In the event that one person commits two or more administrative offences, an administrative offence report is drawn up for each offence separately. The person against whom a report on an administrative offence is drawn up has the right to provide explanations and comments on the content of the report, which are included in the report and certified by the signature of the specified person. An explanation can be added to the protocol separately, which is recorded in the protocol. In the case of refusal of the person against whom a report on an administrative offense is drawn up to provide explanations on the essence of the offence committed, the authorized official shall make a corresponding entry in it. If the offense caused material damage, this is also noted in the administrative offence protocol. Objects and tools of illegal use of natural resources, illegally extracted species, constituting the offence, are seized by authorized officials. The seized firearms and hunting gear are handed over to the bodies (units) of the National Police.

Policy: Financial Sector (Climate-related Disclosures and Other Matters) Amendment Act 2021.
Policy_Content: The Financial Sector (Climate-related Disclosures and Other Matters) Amendment Act 2021 (the Act) amends the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 (the FMC Act), the Financial Reporting Act 2013 and the Public Audit Act 2001. The Act inserts a new Part 7A to the FMC Act which provides a framework to make climate-related disclosure mandatory for certain entities considered to have "higher level of public accountability" under section 461K of the FMC Act. These entities, defined climate reporting entities (CREs), are substantially publicly listed companies and large insurers, banks, non-bank deposit takers and investment managers, and are obliged to comply with certain record-keeping requirements and produce annual climate statements. The Act also establishes offences and liabilities.

Policy: Resolution No. 73 of the Ministry on Emergencies validating Rules and regulations for ensuring nuclear and radiation safety.
Policy_Content: The rules and regulations for ensuring nuclear and radiation safety "General requirements for management systems of operating organizations in order to ensure nuclear and radiation safety" establish general technical requirements for the constituent elements, the procedure for functioning and improving the administrative systems of operating organizations (OO) in terms of ensuring nuclear and radiation safety at all stages of the life cycle of nuclear facilities (NF). Deviations from the requirements of these Rules are allowed for OOs operating at the time of entry into force of these Rules, if plans are developed to bring the administrative systems of such OOs in line with the requirements of these Rules. In order to implement the priority of nuclear and radiation safety, an administrative system must be introduced into the operating system, integrating all control elements in such a way that the processes and actions that ensure compliance with the NF safety requirements are established and carried out taking into account other requirements, including economic requirements, requirements for managers, personnel, labor protection, environmental protection, accounting and control of nuclear materials, physical protection, quality, so that these requirements and requests do not adversely affect the safety of nuclear facilities. The management system should provide for and ensure: (a) integration of all requirements for ensuring the functioning of the OO, including security requirements; (b) an integrated approach to meeting the requirements for the safety of nuclear facilities, the economic activity of the operating organization, labor protection, health and the environment, and physical protection; and (c) planning and implementation on a systematic basis of measures to ensure compliance with safety requirements, as well as control over the implementation of such requirements. The management system should ensure timely identification and integration of safety requirements into the activities of the OO.

Keyword: Radiation, Nuclear energy, Public health, Enforcement/compliance

Policy: Loi n° 43-2021 du 19 octobre 2021 portant loi d’orientation de l’action sociale
Policy_Content: La présente loi d’orientation fixe le cadre de la politique nationale de l’action sociale. Au sens de la présente loi, on entend par « l’action sociale », l’ensemble des moyens mis en œuvre par les différents intervenants du champ social, sous la responsabilité des pouvoirs publics. Ces moyens visent à garantir la cohésion sociale, l’équité, la solidarité nationale, conformément aux principes qui sous-tendent l’action sociale. L’action sociale se déploie au travers des textes législatifs ou réglementaires, des actions et aides visant à prévenir les vulnérabilités, à améliorer les conditions et le cadre de vie des personnes les plus en difficulté, à préserver et à renforcer leur autonomie, à s’adapter à leur environnement socio-économique. L’action sociale intègre l’action humanitaire dans ses aspects de prise en compte des catastrophes et des crises humanitaires. L’action sociale se décline selon les principes suivants : la solidarité nationale, qui s’inscrit dans la perspective de réduire les inégalités et de promouvoir l’égalité des chances, afin d’assurer l’inclusion sociale et de construire une société juste ; l’application équilibrée des volets de prévention, de protection, de prise en charge et de promotion ; la prévention, qui vise à réduire les risques, en se fondant sur l’intervention précoce au niveau des familles et sur les campagnes de sensibilisation au niveau communautaire ; la promotion, qui vise à développer les capacités et les connaissances des personnes, à haut risque, à promouvoir leur autonomisation économique, à assurer leur réinsertion et, dans le cas de personnes vivant en marge de la société, à assurer leur réinsertion familiale et sociale ; la protection et la prise en charge des personnes victimes de violences, de maltraitance, d’exploitation, ou vivant dans les conditions susceptibles de les exposer à de forts risques ; le renforcement du cadre protecteur de la famille aux fins de privilégier la protection, le développement et l’épanouissement de tous ses membres ; la prise en charge et l’accompagnement des personnes victimes des catastrophes ; l’approche communautaire, basée sur une stratégie territoriale globale, intégrée, solidaire et durable, en vue d’une meilleure responsabilisation des populations dans la lutte contre la pauvreté, la prévention des risques sociaux, la médiation et la résolution des problèmes, notamment en milieu rural ; le droit des personnes en général de s’exprimer, et plus particulièrement de celles en situation de haute vulnérabilité, permettant ainsi de prendre en compte les informations, les avis et les opinions de ces personnes ; la responsabilisation des bénéficiaires, en contrepartie des services et des transferts sociaux reçus, afin de promouvoir leur autonomisation et de respecter leurs devoirs envers les autres, notamment les enfants et les femmes ; la protection universelle, qui a pour but de couvrir certaines catégories de dépenses pour tous les individus. La typologie et les prestations y afférentes sont déterminées par voie réglementaire.

Policy: Law No. (23) of 2021 establishing a fund to support the use of renewable energies and raise energy efficiency.
Policy_Content: This Law consisting of 25 Articles aims to establish at the Ministry of Electricity a fund to support the use of renewable energies and raise energy efficiency with the following main objectives (i) promoting the adoption of renewable energy sources among energy consumers and striving to enhance energy efficiency; (ii) increasing the share of renewable energy sources to meet targeted percentages; (iii) curtailing the consumption of fuel and electrical energy across key sectors (domestic, industrial, agricultural, commercial, service, etc.); (iv) mitigating the emission of harmful gases into the environment and mitigating climate change impacts; (v) fostering public awareness about the significance of renewable energies, cultivating a culture of their utilization, and emphasizing their role in sustaining energy resources; (vi) generating new employment opportunities for citizens; (vii) facilitating the transfer and localization of renewable energy technology and energy-efficient equipment. The Fund undertakes the following tasks (i) providing support to beneficiaries; (ii) taking measures to implement studies, activities and events to achieve the Fund’s objectives, in cooperation with the National Energy Research Center and other parties. The means of disbursing the Fund’s funds are determined as follows (i) providing support to beneficiaries in the form of interest-free loans and subsidizing interest on loans; (ii) paying the Fund’s expenses.

Policy: Decree-Law No. 82/2021 establishing the Integrated Management System for Rural Fires in continental territory and defining its operating rules.
Policy_Content: This Decree-Law, consisting of 81 articles divided into seven Chapters, establishes the Integrated Management System for Rural Fires (SGIFR) in the entire National continental territory and defines its operating rules. SGIFR is a set of structures, norms and processes of institutional articulation in the integrated management of rural fire, organization and intervention, relating to planning, preparation, prevention, suppression and relief and post-event, carried out by competent public entities in the integrated management of rural dwellings and by private entities in rural or urban land. SGIFR comprises the following intervention: a) Protection against rural fires, aimed to the safety and safeguard of people, animals and goods; b) Management of rural fire, aimed to the defense and promotion of the value of rural territories, considering their protective role by reducing the conditions for the occurrence and progression of rural fires. SGIFR is based on the principle of specialization of knowledge, using resources with adequate qualification and training for each of the axes of intervention above mentioned, ensuring the concerted action of all resources.
