Policy: Regional Decree No. 299-a constituting protected area of regional significance state nature reserve “Upper river Viga.”
Policy_Content: Protected area of regional significance tourism and recreational area state nature reserve “Upper river Viga” is constituted with a view of conservation and restoration of valuable natural complexes and objects, including habitats of endangered and protected wild fauna and wild flora species. Protected area of regional significance tourism and recreational area state nature reserve “Upper river Viga” performs the following tasks: (a) maintaining the integrity of the ecological system of the watersheds of the Kostroma and Unzha rivers; (b) conservation of the bog complex, which plays a decisive role in maintaining hydrological regime of the Viga River; (c) preservation of valuable swamps and forests; and (d) conservation and restoration of habitats of rare and endangered wild fauna and wild flora species. Protected area of regional significance tourism and recreational area state nature reserve “Upper river Viga” is constituted for unlimited period of time and is classified as complex (landscape). The following activities shall be authorized on the territory of protected area of regional significance tourism and recreational area state nature reserve “Upper river Viga”: (a) haymaking; (b) grazing; (c) educational tourism; (d) recreational and sport hunting and fishing; (e) scientific research; (f) environmental protection; and (g) timber extraction and procurement of non-timber forest resources. The following activities shall be prohibited on the territory of protected area of regional significance tourism and recreational area state nature reserve “Upper river Viga”: (a) felling, except for selective felling and selective sanitary felling except for in case of the outbreak of foci of harmful pests and diseases; (b) application of toxic chemicals as forest protection means, also for scientific research purposes; (c) introduction of alien plant and tree species; (d) commercial hunting; (e) all types of land reclamation; (f) plowing land for agricultural purposes; (g) ruin of nests, clutches, burrows; (h) introduction of plants and animals for the purpose of acclimatization, with the exception of re-acclimatization and restoration of the number of native species; (i) any type construction not related to the functioning of protected area of regional significance tourism and recreational area state nature reserve “Upper river Viga”; (j) allotment of land plots for individual housing construction, gardening or horticulture; (k) traffic off roads and established traffic routes, as well as parking of transport outside specially designated places; (l) pollution of territories and water areas; (m) storage and disposal of manure and industrial and consumption waste; (n) storage of fuels and lubricants, pesticides, mineral fertilizers, placement of cattle burial grounds, cemeteries, dumps of domestic and industrial waste; (o) destruction of hollow trees, large trees with broken tops; (p) tapping trees; (q) industrial harvesting of medicinal raw materials, moss, reeds, forest litter, bark, other technical raw materials; (r) organization of tourist routes without special flooring; (s) organization of tourist camps, bivouacs, making fires outside specially allotted places without agreement with the administration of the reserve “Upper river Viga”; (t) moving through the territory of the reserve “Upper river Viga” using tracked vehicles (with the exception of cases related to ensuring the regime of protection, forestry, reforestation and forest protection works); (u) geological study, exploration and extraction of minerals and groundwater; (v) destruction or damage of barriers, notice boards, stands and other information signs and telltales, as well as equipped ecological trails and recreation areas; and (w) causing harm to natural complexes and their components.

Policy: Second Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC).
Policy_Content: The Second Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) is rooted in the Oman Vision 2040 and the National Energy Strategy to support a gradual transition to a low carbon economy and an energy matrix significantly lower in carbon emissions. This goal will be achieved by slowing GHG emission growth and reduce them by 7% in 2030 (4% based on national efforts, and the remaining 3% would necessitate grants and other forms of concessional financing and assistance). The process will also benefit from the co-benefits such as reduction of air pollutants', creation of jobs, and the transition to a climate-resilient economy and society. The Sultanate adopted a strategic alignment between their NDC adaptation goals with the National Adaptation Plan (NAP) process to foster the resilient climate development's coherence and efficiency. Furthermore, according to the 2040 Vision, the strategic economic direction is toward a diverse and sustainable economy anchored on technology, knowledge, and innovation that operates within integrated frameworks, ensures competitiveness, embraces industrial revolutions, and achieves fiscal sustainability.

Policy: Nationally Determined Contribution.
Policy_Content: This updated Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) is a nationwide sectoral document, in line with Article 4 of the Paris Agreement, representing an incremental contribution beyond the current efforts to reduce greenhouse gas emissions economy-wide between 30-35% relative to the Business-As-Usual (BAU) scenario by 2030. For this purpose, the country is committed to embark on a sustainable development pathway and undertake mitigation measures based on national circumstances and capabilities. Two documents, the National Climate Change Response Strategy (2021) and the Zanzibar Climate Change Strategy (2014) have been already developed to enhance adaptive capacity to climate change and promote adaptation action in order to support long-term climate resilience of social systems and ecosystems and to enhance participation in climate change mitigation activities to contribute to international efforts while ensuring sustainable development. These two strategies were instrumental in the formulation of this Tanzania NDC. Adaptation targets by 2030 are (i) increased access to clean and safe water for the total population in urban and rural areas from 86% and 67.7% respectively in 2015 to 100% by 2030; (ii) reduced impacts of sea-level rise to the island and coastal communities, infrastructure and ecosystems including mangroves; (iii) consider the impacts of climate change in development planning at all levels. As for the mitigation contributions, they are as follows (i) reduce greenhouse gas emissions economy-wide between 30-35% relative to the Business-As-Usual (BAU) scenario; (ii) reduce about 138 - 153 million tons of carbon dioxide. Priority mitigation sectors are energy, transport, forestry, and waste management.

Policy: Rules for the transition from traditional agricultural production to organic farming.
Policy_Content: These Rules of transition from traditional agricultural production to organic farming are developed in accordance with Part 1 of Article 5 of the Law of the Kyrgyz Republic Law No. 65 “On organic agricultural production” and determine the transition from traditional agricultural production to organic farming. These Rules apply to natural or legal persons engaged in organic agricultural production intended as organic crop production and organic livestock breeding. Transition period (conversion) shall be intended the period required for the transition to an organic farming method, during which the requirements established for organic production are applied. All operations carried out during the transition period must meet the requirements of organic agricultural production in accordance with the legislation of the Kyrgyz Republic in the field of organic agricultural production, the rules established by international treaties to which the Kyrgyz Republic is a Party, generally accepted principles, standards, as well as these Rules. Transition period from traditional agricultural production to organic farming shall begin as follows: (a) two years before sowing or planting (for annual plants); (b) two years before grazing or harvesting on pastures or meadows for use as organic feed; and (c) three years before the harvest of organic products (for perennial plants, except fodder plants). Transition period for livestock breeding shall be as follows: for cattle and horses used for meat production (a) 12 months and at least 3⁄4 of their life cycle must pass in an organic management system; calves for meat production (b) six months, after their delivery, only weaned from the mother, under the age of 6 months; for the production of dairy products (c) 90 days during the period of implementation established by the competent authority, then six months; goats and sheep (a) for the production of meat products – six months; (b) for the production of dairy products 90 days during the period of implementation established by the competent authority, then six months; swine (a) for meat production – six months. Poultry/laying birds: (a) for the production of poultry (meat) products – 12 weeks, upon purchase of poultry/birds up to three days old; and (b) for egg production – six weeks. Products obtained from animals may be classified as organic in the case of simultaneous transition to organic farming of all production, including livestock, pastures and (or) any land that is used for animal feed. The total period of transition, both for existing animals and for their offspring, pastures and (or) land plots used for animal feed, may be reduced to 24 months if the animals are fed mainly by products of their own production. Beekeeping products may be sold as organically produced if these rules and the rules/standards for organic production have been observed for at least one year. When choosing breeds, it is necessary to take into account the ability of bees to adapt to local conditions, their viability and resistance to disease. The duration of the transitional period during which the rules of organic agricultural production shall apply, as well as, where appropriate, exceptions to the rules of organic production, shall be: (a) 12 months - when growing sturgeon for caviar; (b) 6 months - when growing sturgeon for the purpose of obtaining aquaculture products, except caviar for alimentary purposes; and (c) 4 months - when growing fish (except sturgeon), invertebrates and algae. Products that are in the process of transition to organic, can be labelled as "the product is in the process of transition to the system organic production" provided that: (a) the producer has been included in the certification program and that production or processing has been carried out in accordance with these Rules and Standards during the previous twelve months; and (b) the label includes the reference "the product is in the process of transition to the system of organic production" or a similar statement in color, size and style of the inscription, which is no more noticeable than the description of the product for sale; the list of ingredients should be in descending order of quantity and indicate which of its ingredients are "at the stage of transition to the system of organic production." The labelling shall reflect the name and/or code number of the officially recognized certification body.

Policy: Regional Law No. 647-Z “On state social assistance.”
Policy_Content: This Regional Law regulates some issues of assigning state social assistance at the expense of the regional budget. Recipients of state social assistance can be poor families, low-income citizens living alone and other categories of citizens. Policy: Pesticide Registration Regulations 2021. S.I. no. 83 of 2021.
Policy_Content: These Regulations prohibit the manufacture, formulation, importation, exportation, advertisement, sale or distribution of pesticide in Nigeria unless the pesticide has been registered with the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) in accordance with the provisions of these Regulations. Bulk importation of pesticides for farm use only shall be exempted from the requirement of an authorization of the Agency. No person shall submit an application for the registration of any pesticide unless such pesticide was manufactured or formulated in an establishment acceptable and approved by the Agency. An efficacy assessment of a pesticide to be introduced into the market shall be carried out to ensure that pesticide approved is efficacious for its intended use. This assessment shall be monitored by the Agency and be carried out for two seasons in two different zones or as may be prescribed by the Agency. The applicant shall state the residue level for the pesticide in all its intended usage in the country and this will be compared with the tolerance level as may be determined by the Agency. The Regulations set out labelling requirements (including instruction for use) for pesticides. Any person who contravenes any of the provisions of these Regulations shall be guilty of an offence and liable on conviction to prescribed penalties.

Policy: Regional Decree No. 290-a constituting protected area of regional significance state nature reserve “Formozovsky”.
Policy_Content: Protected area of regional significance “Formozovsky” is constituted with a view of conservation and restoration of valuable natural complexes and objects, habitats of rare and protected species of wild fauna and wild flora. Protected area of regional significance “Formozovsky” shall perform the following tasks: (a) conservation of the integrity of the ecosystem in the form of connected stripes of light coniferous forests along the valleys of the rivers Vetluga, Nei, Big Kakshi; (b) conservation of representative landscapes of sandy aeolian-glacial plains with pine forests and swamp ecosystems; (c) conservation of the oldest biological research site that recorded the state of landscapes at the beginning of the 20th century, also as an indicator of global changes and regional trends in the development of natural complexes; (d) conservation of the water protection value of forests in the valley of the river Neya; and (e)  conservation of habitats of rare and endangered animal and plant species. The following activities shall be authorized on the territory of protected area of regional significance “Formozovsky”: (a) haymaking; (b) grazing; (c) educational tourism; (d) recreational and sport hunting and fishing; (e) scientific research; (f) environmental protection; and (g) timber extraction and procurement of non-timber forest resources. The following activities shall be prohibited on the territory of protected area of regional significance “Formozovsky”: (a) felling, except for selective felling and selective sanitary felling except for in case of the outbreak of foci of harmful pests and diseases; (b) application of toxic chemicals as forest protection means, also for scientific research purposes; (c) introduction of alien plant and tree species; (d) commercial hunting; (e) all types of land reclamation; (f) plowing land for agricultural purposes; (g) ruin of nests, clutches, burrows; (h) introduction of plants and animals for the purpose of acclimatization, with the exception of re-acclimatization and restoration of the number of native species; (i) any type construction not related to the functioning of protected area of regional significance “Formozovsky”; (j) allotment of land plots for individual housing construction, gardening or horticulture; (k) traffic off roads and established traffic routes, as well as parking of transport outside specially designated places; (l) pollution of territories and water areas; (m) storage and disposal of manure and industrial and consumption waste; (n) storage of fuels and lubricants, pesticides, mineral fertilizers, placement of cattle burial grounds, cemeteries, dumps of domestic and industrial waste; (o) destruction of hollow trees, large trees with broken tops; (p) tapping trees; (q) industrial harvesting of medicinal raw materials, moss, reeds, forest litter, bark, other technical raw materials; (r) organization of tourist routes without special flooring; (s) organization of tourist camps, bivouacs, making fires outside specially allotted places without agreement with the administration of the reserve “Formozovsky”; (t) moving through the territory of the reserve “Formozovsky” using tracked vehicles (with the exception of cases related to ensuring the regime of protection, forestry, reforestation and forest protection works); (u) geological study, exploration and extraction of minerals and groundwater; (v) destruction or damage of barriers, notice boards, stands and other information signs and telltales, as well as equipped ecological trails and recreation areas; and (w) causing harm to natural complexes and their components.

Policy: Federal Law No. 296-FZ “On limiting greenhouse gas emissions”.
Policy_Content: This Federal Law defines the foundations of legal regulation of relations in the field of economic and other activities, which is accompanied by greenhouse gas emissions and is carried out on the territory of the Russian Federation, as well as on the continental shelf, in the Exclusive Economic Zone of the Russian Federation, in the Russian sector of the Caspian Sea. The scope of this Federal Law shall be to create conditions for sustainable and balanced development of the economy of the Russian Federation while reducing the level of greenhouse gas emissions. Principles for limiting greenhouse gas emissions shall be as follows: (a) ensuring sustainable and balanced development of the economy of the Russian Federation while reducing emissions greenhouse gases; (b) obligation of regular reporting by regulated organizations on greenhouse gas emissions; (c) obligation to meet the reduction targets of greenhouse gas emissions; (d) voluntary implementation of climate projects; and (e)  scientific substantiation, consistency and complexity of the approach to limiting greenhouse gas emissions. Measures to limit greenhouse gas emissions include: (a) state accounting of greenhouse gas emissions; (b) setting greenhouse gases emission reduction targets; and (c) support in accordance with the legislation of the Russian Federation of activities to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and increased absorption of greenhouse gases. Target for reducing greenhouse gas emissions for the economy of the Russian Federation is established by the Government of the Russian Federation in accordance with the decrees of the President of the Russian Federation and documents of strategic planning, developed within the framework of goal-setting at the federal level, taking into account the absorption of greenhouse gases in forests and other natural ecological systems and is based on the need to ensure sustainable and balanced development of the economy of the Russian Federation. The report on greenhouse gas emissions must contain information on the amount of greenhouse gas emissions resulting from economic and other activities of regulated organizations, for calendar year, as well as the initial information on the basis of which the amount of these emissions is determined. Liability for untimely submission of such a report, as well as for submission in the specified report of unreliable information is established by the legislation of the Russian Federation. State accounting of greenhouse gases emissions shall be performed in the form of maintaining a register of greenhouse gas emissions, which is a state information system, in accordance with this Federal Law, legislation of the Russian Federation on information, information technologies and protection of information and other regulatory legal acts. Russian Federation shall perform international cooperation in the field of limiting greenhouse gas emissions in accordance with generally recognized principles and norms of international law and international treaties of the Russian Federation.

Unified integrated platform of electronic technical passports includes buildings and structures located in all regions of the country, as well as electronic technical passports of residential (apartment) buildings and shall be regularly updated. Electronic technical passport - an electronic document containing the necessary information on the state of seismic stability of buildings and structures. Formation of electronic technical passports includes systematic collection, processing and analysis of information on the seismic resistance of buildings and structures, as well as apartment buildings. The generated electronic technical passports are used to study the seismic strength of buildings and structures, as well as residential multi-apartment houses in the presence of a seismic hazard forecast, to prepare for an expected earthquake and to mitigate its consequences. The tasks of formation of electronic technical passports are: (a) organization of regular visual and instrumental-technical inspections of buildings and structures located in all regions of the country, as well as in residential (apartment) buildings; (b) conducting research on the seismic strength of buildings and structures, including the construction and operation of buildings and structures in seismic areas, as well as monitoring of damage to buildings and structures after the earthquake; (c) collection of information on seismically weak buildings and structures, as well as residential multi-apartment houses, implementation of appropriate measures to ensure their seismic stability; and (d) prevention of damage to buildings and structures as a result of the earthquake, as well as residential multi-apartment houses, determination of the level of possible damage to their equipment, engineering and communication networks.

Policy: Regulation (EU) 2021/1119 for achieving climate neutrality (European Climate Law).
Policy_Content: This Regulation aims at achieving net zero greenhouse gas emissions for Member States as a whole by 2050, mainly by regulating union-wide greenhouse gas emissions and removals, investing in green technologies and protecting the natural environment. To this end, this Regulation sets out a binding objective of climate neutrality in the Union by 2050 in accordance with the long-term objectives of the Paris Agreement, and establishes a framework for the irreversible and gradual reduction of anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions by sources and enhancement of removals by sinks regulated in Union law. In addition, this Regulation sets out a binding Union target of a net domestic reduction in greenhouse gas emissions for 2030 and 2040. The relevant Union institutions and the Member States shall take the necessary measures at Union and national level to enable the collective achievement of the climate-neutrality objective. A Union strategy on adaptation to climate change in line with the Paris Agreement shall be adopted by the Commission. Furthermore, national measures taken by the Member States, including legislation and adaptation strategies, will be assessed regularly by the Commission to check their consistency with the climate-neutrality objective or adequate to enhance adaptive capacity, in order to strengthen resilience and reduce vulnerability to climate change. This Regulation applies to anthropogenic emissions by sources and removals by sinks of the greenhouse gases listed in Part 2 of Annex V to Regulation (EU) 2018/1999. Public participation will be promoted to enable and empower all parts of society to take action towards a just and socially fair transition to a climate-neutral and climate-resilient society. Finally, this Regulation amends some Articles of the Regulation No. 2018/1999 on the Governance of the Energy Union and Climate Action in pursuit of the Union’s climate-neutrality objective, as well as the objectives and targets of the Energy Union and the long- term Union greenhouse gas emissions commitments consistent with the Paris Agreement.

Policy: Regional Decree No. 274-a constituting protected area of regional significance state nature reserve “Torzatsky”.
Policy_Content: Protected area of regional significance state nature reserve “Torzatsky” is constituted with a view of conservation and restoration of valuable natural complexes and objects, including habitats of rare and protected wild fauna and wild flora species. It performs the following tasks: (a) preservation of the integrity of the ecosystems linking large areas of pine forest landscapes in the central sector of the Kostroma region; (b) preservation of a large complex of surface bogs; (c) preservation of areas of old-growth forests with the participation of larch, coniferous-broad-leaved and pine-larch natural communities; and (d) preservation of habitats of rare and endangered wild fauna and wild flora species. The reserve is classified as complex (landscape) and is constituted for an unlimited period of time without expropriation of land plots. The following activities are authorized on the territory of the reserve: (a) haymaking; (b) grazing; (c) ecological tourism; (d) protection of natural areas; (e) hunting and fishing; (f) scientific research; (g) timber extraction, tapping of trees, and procurement of non-timber forest resources; and (h) reserve forests. The following activities shall be prohibited on the territory of the reserve: (a) felling, except for authorized types of felling; (b) use of toxic chemicals for the protection and protection of forests, including for scientific purposes; (c) introduction (species) of trees, shrubs, vines, other forest plants that do not grow in this forest area, in the course of reforestation; (d) commercial hunting; (e) all types of land reclamation works, with the exception of cultural and technical measures on agricultural lands, phosphorite, liming; (f) plowing land for agricultural purposes; (g) ruin of nests, clutches, holes; (h) introduction of plants and animals for the purpose of acclimatization, with the exception of measures for re-acclimatization and restoration of the number of native species; (i) construction of industrial facilities, buildings, residential buildings, paved roads, construction of structures not related to the operation of the reserve; (j) allotment of land plots for individual housing construction, gardening or horticulture; (k) traffic off roads and established traffic routes, as well as parking of vehicles outside specially designated places; (l) types of activities that can lead to pollution of territories and water areas; (m) storage of manure and industrial and domestic waste; (n) placement of zones for storage and disposal of industrial, domestic and agricultural waste; (o) placement of warehouses for fuels and lubricants, pesticides, mineral fertilizers, cattle burial grounds, cemeteries, landfills for household and industrial waste; (p) destruction of oak, larch, juniper (tree form), black alder, linden, fir, maple, elm, hazel, as well as their undergrowth, or actions that may lead to their destruction; (q) destruction of hollow trees, large trees with broken tops; (r) tapping of trees; (s) industrial harvesting of medicinal raw materials, moss, reeds, forest litter, bark, other technical raw materials; (t) organization of tourist camps, bivouacs, making fires outside specially designated places without the consent of the administration of the reserve; (u) movement through the territory of the reserve using caterpillar vehicles (with the exception of cases related to ensuring the protection regime, conducting forestry, reforestation and forest protection work); (v) geological study, exploration and extraction of minerals and groundwater; and (w) destruction or damage to barriers, notice boards, stands and other information signs and indicators, as well as equipped ecological trails and recreation areas.

Policy: Regulation on Packaging Waste Management.
Policy_Content: This Regulation lays down provisions for the development and protection of the environment in a sustainable manner, relating to: (I) responsibilities and liabilities of businesses for the production and marketing of packages with certain standards, conditions and qualifications; (II) prevention of the formation of packaging waste, and reduction of the amount of unavoidable packaging waste to be disposed of by using reuse, recycling and recovery methods; (III) management of packaging wastes within a significant management system, including deposit management and zero-waste management systems; (IV) implementation of a deposit management system; and (V) activities to be carried out by the Turkish Environment Agency in line with its duties and authorities in the management of packaging and packaging wastes. This Regulation shall apply to all packages and their wastes released in the market. This Regulation aims to ensure the collection of packaging wastes within the scope of the zero-waste management system in line with the provisions of the Zero Waste Regulation. Furthermore, the responsibilities and liabilities of individuals and businesses are determined within the Polluter Pays Principle and Extended Producer Liability concepts. The mandatory deposit management will be implemented as of 1 January 2022 for glass, polyethylene terephthalate and aluminum packages of drinks. Moreover, this Regulation sets out specific targets for recycling and recovering in general as well as for certain types of products.

Policy: Presidential Decree No. 240 “On administrative procedures carried out in relation to business entities.”
Policy_Content: The President, in order to streamline the regulation of business and other economic activities, as well as to further improve the procedure for carrying out administrative procedures, decrees to determine that the principles for implementing administrative procedures in relation to business entities (legal entities and individual entrepreneurs) are: (a) availability and priority of taking into account the interests of business entities; (b) the inadmissibility of refusal to accept an application from a business entity and carry out an administrative procedure on grounds not provided for by legislative acts, resolutions of the Council of Ministers of the Republic of Belarus and resolutions of the Board of the National Bank; (c) determination of the list of documents and (or) information submitted by a business entity to carry out an administrative procedure; (d) ensuring the greatest possible convenience in carrying out administrative procedures, including through consolidation in the “one window” service; (e) maximum use of information technology in the process implementation of administrative procedures, including by converting them into electronic form; and (f) proportionality of the general administrative burden on business entities to the actual needs of regulating business and other economic activities through the implementation of administrative procedures. Regulatory body shall be intended a state body, other organization, including those not subordinate to the Council of Ministers of the Republic of Belarus, whose competence includes the implementation of state policy in the relevant area of public relations. The Ministry of Economy shall be responsible for the registration of information and data related to business entities and individual entrepreneurs, and keeping the state register. This Presidential Decree shall not be applicable to the following fields: (a) specific goods related to works and services; (b) expropriation and allotment of land plots; (c) ensuring nuclear and radiation safety; (d) liquidation of the consequences of emergency situation; (e) state secrets; and (f) registration and liquidation (cancellation) of business entities and individual entrepreneurs.

Policy: Regulation (EU) 2021/1057 establishing the European Social Fund Plus (ESF+) and repealing Regulation (EU) No 1296/2013.
Policy_Content: This Regulation establishes the European Social Fund Plus (ESF+) for the period 2021 to 2027 to support investments in people and systems in the policy areas of employment, education and social inclusion. The ESF+ aims to support Member States to ensure equal opportunities and access to the labour market, fair and quality working conditions, social protection and inclusion, in particular focussing on quality and inclusive education and training, lifelong learning, investment in children and young people and access to basic services. The specific objectives of the ESF+ are: (I) improving access to employment and activation measures for all jobseekers, in particular young people, long-term unemployed and disadvantaged groups, (II) modernizing labour market institutions and services to assess and anticipate skills needs, (III) promoting an equal participation labour market with a gender-sensitive approach, equal working conditions, and a better work-life balance, (IV) improving the quality, inclusiveness, effectiveness and labour market relevance of education and training systems, (V) promoting equal access to and completion of quality and inclusive education and training, in particular for disadvantaged groups, (VI) promoting the socio-economic integration of marginalised communities and third-country nationals, (VII) enhancing equal and timely access to quality, sustainable and affordable services, (VIII) promoting social integration of people at risk of poverty or social exclusion, including the most deprived persons and children, (IX) providing food and/or basic material assistance to the most deprived persons, including children, and taking accompanying measures supporting their social inclusion. ESF+ contributes to the promotion of equality between women and men to foster equality of treatment and opportunities between women and men in all areas. Moreover, this Regulation will contribute to mainstream climate actions and to the achievement of an overall target of 30 % of Union budget expenditure supporting climate objectives.

Policy: United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act S.C. 2021, c. 14.
Policy_Content: The purposes of this Act are to affirm the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples as a universal international human rights instrument with application in Canadian law; and to provide a framework for the Government of Canada’s implementation of the Declaration. Firstly the Act establishes that the Government of Canada must, in consultation and cooperation with Indigenous peoples, take all measures necessary to ensure that the laws of Canada are consistent with the Declaration. Then the Act requires that the Minister must, in consultation and cooperation with Indigenous peoples and with other federal ministers, prepare and implement an action plan to achieve the objectives of the Declaration. The action plan must include measures to: a) address injustices, combat prejudice and eliminate all forms of violence, racism and discrimination, including systemic racism and discrimination, against Indigenous peoples and Indigenous elders, youth, children, women, men, persons with disabilities and gender-diverse persons and two-spirit persons, and (ii) promote mutual respect and understanding as well as good relations, including through human rights education; and (b) measures related to monitoring, oversight, recourse or remedy or other accountability measures with respect to the implementation of the Declaration. This Law applies to: (a) unfair trading practices, where agricultural and food products are sold by suppliers whose annual turnover in the previous financial year between EUR 1 million and EUR 350 million per year, and where agricultural and food products are purchased by purchasers, regardless of their annual turnover during the previous financial year; (b) unfair trading practices, where agricultural and food products are sold by suppliers whose annual turnover in the previous financial year is not exceeding EUR 2 million, purchasers of agricultural products and foodstuffs whose annual turnover during the preceding financial year is more than EUR 2 million; (c) suppliers with an annual turnover in the preceding financial year of more than EUR 2 million but not more than EUR 1 million for purchasers of agricultural and food products of which the annual turnover during the preceding financial year is more than EUR 1 million; (c) suppliers whose annual turnover in the preceding financial year exceeds l EUR 1 million, but not more than EUR 50 million, for purchasers of agricultural and food products whose the annual turnover for the preceding financial year is more than EUR 50 million; (d) suppliers with an annual turnover of more than EUR 50 million but not more than EUR 150 million for purchasers of agricultural and food products with the annual turnover for the preceding financial year is more than EUR 150 million; and (e) suppliers with an annual turnover in the preceding financial year of more than EUR 150 million but not more than EUR 350 million for purchasers of agricultural and food products with the annual turnover for the preceding financial year is more than EUR 350 million. This Act shall apply to the sale of agricultural and food products when supplier of agricultural and food products or a buyer of these products, or both are located in the European Union. It shall not be applicable to supply and purchase contracts of agricultural and food products with consumers and to supply and purchase contracts of food products between agricultural cooperatives and small partnerships and their members. When the contract of sale provides for regular agricultural and food products supply, unfair commercial practices where the buyer is late in paying the supplier: (a) for agricultural and food products, the list of which is approved by the authorized institution of the Republic of Lithuania Law on the Settlement of Agricultural Products, Article 5 (2), and perishable agricultural products and foodstuffs as within 30 calendar days from the delivery of these products specified in the sales contract the end of the period, including the valuation period for these products, or longer than 30 calendar days from the date of that delivery, including the pricing of those products to the date on which the due amount is determined, whichever is the later; (b) for agricultural and food products not classified in item (a) of this paragraph for products: (1) where the contract of sale is concluded between a supplier and a purchaser who is in the public domain longer than established by Article 6 (2) and (2) of the Law on the Settlement of Agricultural Products, considering the time limits set out in paragraph 3; and (3) where the contract of sale is concluded between a supplier and a buyer other than those referred to in this item - within 60 calendar days from the date specified in the contract of sale  by the end of the delivery period for those products, including the pricing period for those products, or no later than 60 calendar days after the end of that delivery period, by the date of determination of the amount payable.

The States Parties to this Treaty, in the context of conservation and sustainable management of forest ecosystems in Central Africa, undertake to: Inscribe in their national priorities the conservation and sustainable management of forests, as well as the management of the environment; Adopt harmonized national policies on forests and accelerate the introduction of instruments for regulating the exploitation of forests; Putting in place measures aimed at reconciling actions in favour of conservation and sustainable management of forest ecosystems; Establish, lasting mechanisms for financing the development of the Forestry Sector; etc. For the execution of this Treaty, an international sub-regional organization “Commission on Forests of Central Africa” is created, (COMIFAC). COMIFAC is an organization charged with guiding, harmonizing and monitoring forestry and environmental policies in Central Africa.

Policy: Kuwait National Implementation Plan to the Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants
Policy_Content: This National Implementation Plan is a nationwide sectoral document aiming at (i) describing the actions that Kuwait has undertaken regarding the inventory, management, and reduction of the presence of POPs; (ii) proposing actions that Kuwait will undertake in order to manage and eliminate POPs, as well as for preventing these chemicals from entering the environment; (iii) informing the Conference of the Parties and Kuwait’s stakeholders about the national initiatives and projects designed to meet the requirements of the Stockholm Convention. The overall objective of the sound management of POPs and hazardous chemicals, is to strengthen the national capacity and capability to deliver a comprehensive assessment of the threats posed by chemicals, reduce and where possible, eliminate the exposure of the populations and the environment, to POPs and hazardous chemicals. Consequently, it is necessary to (i) eliminate or reduce POPs releases; (ii) carry out environmentally sound management of stockpiles of POPs containing wastes and contaminated sites that pose risks to human health and the environment; (iii) integrate environmental considerations and pollution prevention into the Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) of the 2030 Sustainable Development Agenda. The current NIP has assessed the 28 POPs listed up to 2017 (COP8) and also includes dicofol (POP 29) listed in 2019 (COP9), while excludes PFOA, also listed in 2019. The document includes cross-sectoral issues, such as gender considerations, considering that efforts to ensure sound management of chemicals, including POPs have important gender dimensions, because in daily life, men, women, and children are exposed to different kinds of chemicals in varying concentrations. Time frames for its implementation are short-term (2 years and less), medium-term (3 to 5 years) and long-term (10 years).

Policy: National Five Year Development Plan 2021/22–2025/26.
Policy_Content: This Third National Five Year Development Plan (FYDP III) for the period 2021/2026 is a nationwide multisector document aiming at achieving the goals set in the National Development Vision 2025. The main areas included in the Plan are (i) increasing the country’s capacity for production; (ii) building a competitive economy that will stimulate the country’s participation in trade and investment; and (iii) stimulate human development. In achieving the priority areas of the Plan, the strategic objectives of the FYDP III are (i) improve key productive infrastructures including roads, railways, water, and air transport as well as reliable access to energy; (ii) strengthen the business and investment enabling environment through effective policies to facilitate free private-sector competition; and (iii) improve and strengthen education and training systems, including reforming the education curriculum in line with labor market demand as well as integrating research and development with productive economic activities. To achieve these objectives, main efforts will be directed to (i) identification of interventions designed to improve the competitiveness of the country (also through a transformative participation of the private sector and non-state actors in the competitive economy); (ii) interventions to further deepen industrialization; (iii) trade and investment to increase Tanzania’s participation in global and regional trade; (iv) social development, emphasizing coverage, equity and quality of services to attain inclusive economy; and (v) skills development.

Policy: Regional Law No. 746-oz “On the powers of state authorities of the Amur region in the field of ensuring biological safety.”
Policy_Content: The scope of this Regional Law is the delimitation of powers between regional state bodies in the field of biological safety. Regional Assembly shall have the following powers: (a) adoption of regional normative legal acts in the field of biological safety; and (b) implementation of other powers in accordance with federal and regional legislation. Regional Government shall have the following powers: (a) participation in the implementation of state policy of the Russian Federation in the field of ensuring biological safety; (b) adoption of normative legal acts in the field of ensuring biological safety; (c) appointment of the regional state executive bodies authorized in the field of ensuring biological safety; (d) coordination of activities of the regional state executive bodies in the field of ensuring biological safety; and (e) other powers envisaged by the federal and regional legislation. Regional state executive bodies authorized in the field of ensuring biological safety, within their competence, shall have the following powers: (a) participation in the planning and implementation of anti-epidemic, antiepizootic, antiepiphytotic measures; (b) participation in the monitoring of biological risks and in assessing the effectiveness of the implementation of activities, aimed at ensuring biological safety, on the regional territory; (c) information of local governments and the population about the implemented on the regional territory of activities aimed at ensuring biological safety; (d) provision of citizens and organizations with information about the state of protection of the population and the environment from the impact of dangerous biological factors, on the undertaken measures aimed at protection of the population and environment from the effects of hazardous biological factors, and prevention of biological risks (hazards); (e)  acceptance of proposals from citizens on measures to ensure biological safety in the region; and (f) other powers in accordance with federal and regional  legislation.

Policy: Ley de Mitigación y Adaptación al Cambio Climático y Desarrollo Sustentable para la Ciudad de México.
Policy_Content: La presente Ley establece el marco normativo para el Distrito Federal en materia de mitigación de gases de efecto invernadero, adaptación al cambio climático y desarrollo sustentable. Esta Ley tiene por objeto: I. Garantizar el derecho de toda persona a un medio ambiente sano para su desarrollo y bienestar; II. Definir los principios, criterios, instrumentos y órganos para la aplicación en la Política en la Ciudad de México en materia de cambio climático; III. Establecer la concurrencia de competencias, atribuciones y facultades de la Ciudad de México, sus dependencias, entidades y Alcaldías, a fin de que se apliquen de manera coordinada y concertada en todas las etapas de planeación, ejecución, seguimiento y evaluación de las políticas públicas para la mitigación y adaptación al cambio climático; IV. Establecer las bases para desarrollar políticas públicas de la Ciudad de México y Alcaldías con criterios transversales en materia de resiliencia, mitigación y adaptación al cambio climático; V.  Instrumentar los  mecanismos que promuevan la participación informada,  incluyente, equitativa, diferenciada, corresponsable, efectiva y solidaria de la sociedad en materia de resiliencia, mitigación y adaptación al cambio climático; VI. Asegurar que las acciones de mitigación y adaptación al cambio climático coadyuven al equilibrio de la biodiversidad, los ecosistemas y sus servicios, para proteger y mejorar la calidad de vida de la población;VII. Reducir el riesgo y las condiciones de vulnerabilidad de la población en zonas rurales y urbanas, de la infraestructura, de los sistemas productivos y de los ecosistemas, frente a los efectos adversos del cambio climático, mejorar su resiliencia,así como crear y fortalecer las capacidades locales de prevención, acción y respuesta; VIII. Fomentar una cultura ambiental ciudadana, por medio del acceso a información y promoción de la participación, que favorezca la transformación de patrones, hábitos y costumbres de producción y consumo, amigables con el medio ambiente y la sustentabilidad; IX. Fomentar la educación, investigación, desarrollo y transferencia de tecnología, la innovación, comunicación y difusión en materia de resiliencia, mitigación y adaptación al cambio climático; X. Contribuir a frenar los procesos de deterioro ambiental, especialmente en las áreas con mayores condiciones de vulnerabilidad de la Ciudad de México, a través de la conservación de la biodiversidad, protección y aprovechamiento sustentable de los ecosistemas, conservación de suelos y gestión integral de los recursos hidrológicos; XI Diseñar políticas que contribuyan a la restauración de áreas degradadas y de los servicios de los ecosistemas, especialmente para aprovisionamiento de agua y alimentos; XII Promover la conservación y manejo sustentable de los ecosistemas de la Ciudad de México para reducir las emisiones por deforestación y degradación forestal y del suelo, así como para aumentar la captura de CyGEI y su almacenamiento en sumideros y reservorios, y XIII. Contribuir al cumplimiento de las obligaciones internacionales, así como las metas nacionales a mediano y largo plazo en materia de cambio climático.

Policy: Law No. 379-VI “On public-private partnership.”
Policy_Content: The objectives of this Law are to regulate relations in the field of public-private partnership, as well as the creation of legal conditions for the concentration of material, financial, intellectual, scientific, technical and other resources, ensuring a balance of interests and risks, attraction of funds from extra-budgetary sources for the implementation of projects, plans and development programs related to infrastructure facilities. Public-private partnership shall be intended legally formalized for a certain period mutually beneficial cooperation between public and private partners, based on combining their resources for the preparation and implementation of a public-private partnership project. State partner shall be Turkmenistan, on behalf of which operate executive bodies, as well as other bodies (organizations) authorized by the Cabinet of Ministers of Turkmenistan. Private partner shall be intended a legal entity (except for a legal entity, in the authorized capital of which a share, exceeding 50 percent belongs to the state), foreign organization and natural persons engaged in entrepreneurial activity without forming a legal entity - an individual entrepreneur who is a party to a public-private partnership agreement. The basic principles of public-private partnership are: (a) the rule of law; (b) the social orientation of the regulation of economic activity; (c) fair competition; (d) ensuring a balance of interests and risks between public and private partners; (e) equality of rights for public and private partners; (f) environmental protection; (g) transparency of rules and procedures in the implementation of public-private partnerships; and (h) the effectiveness of public-private partnership projects. The main directions of state policy in the field of public-private partnership are: (a) stimulating economic growth and ensuring sustainable development of Turkmenistan; (b) implementation of state programs in the field of public-private partnerships; (c) assistance in the formation, restoration, operation, maintenance of socio-economic infrastructure; (d) improving the quality of operation and maintenance of socio-economic infrastructure; (e) digitalization and improvement of the quality of public services, as well as expanding access to them; (f) creating conditions for attracting private sector finance, including foreign investment; and (g) state support for scientific research, the introduction of modern methods and technologies for the development and improvement of the institutional and legal foundations of public-private partnerships. This Law consists of IX Chapters divided into 38 Articles. Chapter I lays down general provisions. Chapter II establishes state regulation of public-private partnerships. Chapter III determines the parties to public-private partnership agreements, rights and obligations thereof. Chapter IV regards initiation and preparation of the projects of public-private partnerships. Chapter V regards selection of a private partner. Chapter VI defines public-private partnership agreement. Chapter VII establishes guarantees of the rights of private partner and creditor. Chapter VIII regards monitoring and reporting of project implementation of public-private partnership. Chapter IX lays down conclusive provisions.

Policy: Resolution of the Council of Ministers No. 68/2021 approving the National Strategy for the Sea 2021-2030.
Policy_Content: This Resolution of the Council of Ministers approves the National Strategy for the Sea 2021-2030. The sea is one of the most important identity marks of Portugal. A healthy ocean is a fundamental condition for Portuguese society to benefit from, including the sustainable, circular and inclusive blue economy. In a decade marked by the imperative of global threats, such as climate change, loss of biodiversity and ecosystem integrity, new forms of pollution and ocean acidification, Portugal is called to play an active role in the search for global solutions. Scientific research allows us to identify ways to protect vulnerable species and ecosystems, safeguard cultural heritage and optimize economic activities, working as an engine for innovation, which is fundamental for economic development and job creation. The security dimension is crucial to respond to threats, preventing and acting in situations that put the marine environment, economic activities and human life at sea at risk. Thus, the vision of this strategy is based on promoting a healthy ocean to enhance sustainable blue development, the well-being of the Portuguese. Strategic objectives for the decade: Portugal and the world are facing major global challenges today and in the next 10 years. Climate change, the over-exploitation of the planet's natural resources and the decline of its biodiversity, hunger and thirst, human and ecosystem health and the loss of goods and knowledge linked to cultural heritage are actual challenges.

Policy: Regional Law No. 33-OZ “On state support of agricultural production.”
Policy_Content: This Regional Law regulates relations in the field of state support of agricultural production on the regional territory. Agro-industrial complex shall be intended aggregate of agricultural commodity producers, organizations and individual entrepreneurs, carrying out primary and (or) subsequent processing of agricultural commodities and trade thereof, providing services (performing work) in the field of animal husbandry, crop production, veterinary medicine, technical and other types of services, scientific organizations and educational organizations providing training of personnel in the field of agriculture, whose activities are interconnected with each other in technological, economic and organizational relationship. Recipients of state support shall be the following categories: (a) agricultural producers; (b) organizations and individual entrepreneurs performing primary and (or) subsequent processing of agricultural commodities and trade thereof; (c) organizations and individual entrepreneurs providing services to agricultural producers, which include in accordance with the All-Russian Classifier of Types of Economic activities ancillary activities in the field of crop production and post-harvest processing of agricultural commodities, including field preparation, sowing, cultivation of crops, harvesting, protection of plants from agricultural pests, preparation of crops for storage and trade on the market, and storage of agricultural commodities; (d) other organizations and individual entrepreneurs of agro-industrial complex; (e)  persons filling the positions of heads of agricultural organizations; (f) workers of the agro-industrial complex, including young specialists; and (g) citizens of the Russian Federation living and working in rural areas or who have expressed a desire to move to a permanent residence in rural areas and work there. State support shall be granted in the following forms: (a) provision of financial support; (b) provision of support in the development of human resources potential; and (c) provision of information and extension services.

Policy: Decree-Law No. 46/2021 establishing principles and rules for the activity of Energy Service Companies (ESE).
Policy_Content: This Decree-Law, consisting of 30 articles divided into six Chapters, establishes principles and rules for the activity of Energy Service Companies (ESE). In particular it: a) Creates the conditions for the development of a highly specialized ESE market that can provide its services with quality, safety and effectiveness; b) Establishes the legal regime applicable to the ESE, regulating the access and exercise of the activity; c) Defines the general guidelines that should guide the performance of energy audits, the preparation of Energy Sustainability Plans (PSE) and Energy Performance Contracts (CDE); and d) Provides for the creation of the Energy Services Management System (SIGSE). The Statute applies to all private entities that wish to provide energy services to final consumers, in particular energy efficiency services and local energy production services, based on CDE. Policy: Regional Order No. 41-P of the Forestry and Hunting Agency validating the Regulation on the procedure of registration of conservation obligation related to nature monuments of regional significance.
Policy_Content: This Regional Order establishes the procedure of registration of conservation obligation related to nature monuments of regional significance. The Agency shall draw up conservation obligations for nature monuments on the basis of proposals received from owners and tenants of land plots on which nature monuments are located, who undertake obligations to ensure the regime of special protection of nature monuments. Draft conservation obligation is prepared by the specialists of the authorized structural subdivision of the Agency in accordance with the form contained in the Annex. Conservation obligation shall be executed in two copies (one copy for each party).  Conservation obligation is signed by the Head of the Agency or a person acting on his/her behalf and certified by a seal. Conservation obligation is sent to the conservatory person for review and signing in two copies by registered mail with notification within 5 working days or is delivered against signature directly to the conservatory person. Conservatory person shall review and sign the conservation obligation within 10 working days. After signing by the conservatory person, one copy of the signed conservation obligation shall remain with the conservatory person, while the second copy shall be sent to the Agency within 5 working days by registered mail with notification. Annex 1 contains Model form of certificate of nature monument of regional significance.

Policy: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/1760 supplementing Regulation (EU) 2019/6 of the European Parliament and of the Council by establishing the criteria for the designation of antimicrobials to be reserved for the treatment of certain infections in humans.
Policy_Content: This Regulation establishes the criteria for the designation of the antimicrobials which are to be reserved for treatment of certain infections in humans, which are set out in the Annex. Those criteria should allow to identify those antimicrobials that are of high importance to preserve human health and that should therefore be considered for use in human medicine exclusively. The criteria should also enable to identify those antimicrobials, whose use in animals could accelerate the spread of antimicrobial resistance, or present a risk thereof, by allowing for the transmission of resistance, which may include cross-resistance or co-selection of resistance to other antimicrobials, from animals to humans. Finally, the criteria should allow to identify antimicrobials that do not represent an essential need for animal health, and whose absence of use in veterinary medicine would not lead to any significant negative impact on animal health.

Policy: Regional Law No. 745-OZ “On regulation of some issues related to apiculture.”
Policy_Content: This Regional Law regulates the issues of apiculture. The main directions of the regional policy in the development of apiculture shall be as follows: (a) stimulating the development of beekeeping in the region, increasing the number of physical and legal persons involved in apiculture; (b) preservation and multiplication of honey yielding wild plants that are sources of apiculture; (c) education of careful attitude to bees, protection of bees; and (d) other areas in accordance with the federal legislation. Financial support of apiculture in the form subsidies shall be allocated from the regional budget. The placement of stationary apiaries by natural and legal persons involved in apiculture on land plots belonging to them by right of ownership or other rights, envisaged by the Russian Federation, as well as on land of forest fund shall be performed in accordance with the Russian forest and land legislation in conformity with veterinary regulations. In order to ensure productive keeping of bee families and effective pollination of agricultural entomophilous plants natural and legal persons involved in apiculture have the right to place non-stationary (nomadic) apiaries near honey collection sources. The placement of non-stationary apiaries shall be performed in accordance with the Russian forest and land legislation in conformity with veterinary regulations. The owner of an apiary shall be issued veterinary and sanitary certificate. The issuance of veterinary and sanitary certificate shall be performed at the location of the apiary.

Policy: Governmental Decree No. 783 validating Requirements for the content of the action plan for reproduction of agricultural land fertility and the procedure for its preparation.
Policy_Content: This Governmental Decree sets out requirements for the content of the action plan for reproduction of agricultural land fertility and establishes the procedure for its preparation. Action plan is drafted in the form of a single document consisting of text and tabular sections. The textual part of the plan shall contain: (a) information about the owner of the land plot, land tenant, landlord and lessee of agricultural land plot, on which in the corresponding year in accordance with federal state budgetary institutions subordinate to the Ministry of Agriculture of the Russian Federation, were performed soil, geobotanical and other surveys of agricultural land related to: (1) for physical person - surname, name and patronymic (the last - if available); (2) for legal entity - full or abbreviated (if any) name, main state registration of the identification number of the legal entity, the date of its assignment and the name of the body, which made the decision to register a legal entity; and (3) for individual entrepreneur, peasant (farm) economy, created without the formation of a legal persons, - last name, first name and patronymic (the last - if any), main state registration number of the record of an individual entrepreneur, taxpayer identification number; (b) postal and e-mail addresses provided by the owner of land plot, land tenant, land owner and lessee of agricultural land plot, but in case of failure to provide information by the specified persons about address - legal address (for a legal entity) or location address/residence (for physical person); (c) list of the surveys carried out, the period of their performance, surveyed area; (d) results of the surveys (list of surveyed indicators of the state of agricultural land fertility; (e) comparative analysis of survey results (if available results of previous surveys); and (f) substantiation for the performance of arrangements. The tabular part of the plan is a schedule of implementation of activities, which shall contain: (a) serial number of the land plot destined for planned arrangements; (b) location of land plot; (c) cadastral number of land plot; (d) land area (hectares); (e) list of arrangements; (f) works performed within the framework of the performance of arrangements; and (g) the timing of the arrangements.

Policy_Content: La présente loi détermine les principes fondamentaux du contrôle des pollutions et des nuisances. La loi précise aussi que c’est le conseil des ministres qui fixe les modalités d’application de cette disposition, la liste des projets soumis à l’étude et à la notice d’impact environnemental et social, précise le contenu des procédures de toutes les activités susceptibles de porter atteinte à l’environnement et à la qualité du cadre de vie qui doivent être soumises à une étude ou à la notice d’impact environnemental et social et détermine les conditions d’exécution de l’audit environnementale (tout travail, tout aménagement et tout ouvrage industriel, Agricole, minier, artisanal, commercial ou de transport dont l’activité peut être source de pollution, de nuisance ou de dégradation de l’environnement). Cette loi confirme l’accès à l’information à toute personne, définit la notion des déchets et détermine les différents déchets qui peuvent être produits (domestiques solides, domestiques liquides, agricoles, biomédicaux, dangereux, spéciaux, industriels), la pollution atmosphérique et les odeurs incommodantes, les bruits nuisibles et les substances chimiques. Aussi, elle détaille la procédure de contrôle par les autorités compétentes (qui sont les agents assermentés de la Direction Nationale de l’Assainissement et du Contrôle des Pollutions et de Nuisances (DNACPN)), la constatation, l’investigation et l’établissement des infractions à appliquer en cas de transgression.

Policy: Investment Law No.18 of 2021.
Policy_Content: This Law consisting of 51 articles divided into XII Chapters aims at (i) creating a competitive investment environment to attract capital and benefit from various expertise and specializations; (ii) expanding the production base to increase job opportunities and raising economic growth rates, which will have a positive impact on the increase in national income, leading to comprehensive and sustainable development; (iii) simplifying the procedures to obtain a license from the Syrian Investment Authority, whose main feature is tax exemptions for projects of national interest. Article 6 establishes the Supreme Investment Council, chaired by the Prime Minister, with the following main powers (i) studying and approving investment proposals; (ii) making decisions related to dealing with cases related to investors' problems; (iii) proposing the creation of special economic zones after coordination with the concerned authorities; (iv) studying and approving the procedures manuals; (v) studying and updating project licensing mechanisms in coordination with the concerned authorities; (vi) canceling exemptions, benefits or facilities granted to the project; (vii) procedural matters related to the work of the Syrian Investment Authority, a public body of an administrative nature established under article 8 that replaces the newly created in 2007 with its rights and obligations. Article 16 establishes the Investor Services Center which includes representatives of all public agencies concerned with investment, and acts as a single window for investment as well as (i) receiving and studying investor requests for an investment license; (ii) issuing all the licenses and approvals necessary to start the project; (iii) granting an investment license to start implementing the investment project; (iv) providing technical support, advice, data and information necessary to the investor throughout the life of the project; (v) registering companies and issuing records with the concerned authorities. The incentives provided by the Law regard (i) customs incentives (art.20); tax incentives (art.21); non-tax incentives (art.22). The tax and customs duty incentives in certain cases reach the level of complete tax exemption for a project. Development projects will benefit from a 75% discount on income taxes for 10 years. Some industrial projects benefit from exemptions ranging from 50% to 75% on income taxes, including those about technology, medicine, pharmaceuticals, renewable energy, waste recycling, and crafts. Imports of equipment, machinery, assembly lines, and transport systems will be processed free of duties and tariffs. Agricultural projects will not be taxed on profits.

Policy: EU Action Plan: 'Towards Zero Pollution for Air, Water and Soil'.
Policy_Content: This EU Action Plan is a policy at the EU level with a cross-sectoral approach. The timeframe of the policy is 10 years between 2021 and 2030. The objective of this policy is to reduce: (I) the negative impacts of air pollution on health; (II) noise pollution due to transport; (III) the threat of air pollution on biodiversity; (IV) nutrient losses, the use and risk of chemical pesticides and hazardous chemicals, and the sale of antimicrobials for farmed animals and in aquaculture; (V) marine pollution due to plastic litter and microplastics released into the environment; and (VI) total waste generation. Moreover, this action plan also sets out key actions for other European Green Deal initiatives, including the chemicals strategy for sustainability, for the period of 2021-2024.

Policy_Content: Constitue une activité touristique, toute activité commerciale menée de façon durable et responsable, par une personne physique ou morale qui respecte et préserve à long terme les ressources naturelles, culturelles et sociales et, concourant à la satisfaction des besoins des personnes qui voyagent pour leur agrément ou des motifs professionnels. Est considéré comme établissement de tourisme, toute entreprise dont l’objet social consiste à exercer une activité touristique. Sont des établissements de tourisme : les établissements d’hébergement ; les établissements de restauration ; et les stations touristiques ; les sociétés de transport touristique ; les agences de voyage et de tourisme ; les agences et bureaux d’information touristique ; les sites touristiques aménagés ; et tous autres établissements assimilés ou connexes. Policy: Ley Orgánica de Protección de Datos Personales
Policy_Content: La presente Ley tiene el objeto y finalidad de garantizar el ejercicio del derecho a la protección de datos personales, que incluye el acceso y decisión sobre información y datos de este carácter, así como su correspondiente protección. Para dicho efecto regula, prevé y desarrolla principios, derechos, obligaciones y mecanismos de tutela. Se define el ámbito de aplicación material y territorial. Se establecen los integrantes del sistema de protección de datos personales y las condiciones que deben cumplir para que el tratamiento sea legítimo y lícito. Se establecen los principios de la Ley. Se establecen los derechos específicos: derecho a la información, derecho de acceso, derecho de rectificación y actualización, derecho de eliminación, derecho de oposición, derecho a la portabilidad, derecho a la suspensión del tratamiento, derecho a no ser objeto de una decisión basada única o parcialmente en valoraciones automatizadas, derecho de niñas(os) y adolescentes a no ser objeto de una decisión basada única o parcialmente en valoraciones atomizadas, derecho de consulta, y el derecho a la educación digital.  También se establecen excepciones a los derechos de rectificación, actualización, eliminación, oposición, anulación y portabilidad. Se clasifican categorías especiales de datos. Se establecen los requisitos para la transferencia o comunicación y acceso a datos personales por terceros. Se establecen las obligaciones para asegurar la seguridad de datos personales. Se establecen los requerimientos directos y el procedimiento administrativo. Se establecen medidas correctivas, infracciones y el régimen sancionatorio. Se establece la autoridad de protección de datos personales.

Policy: Environmental Management (Control and Management of Electrical and Electronic Equipment Waste) Regulations, 2021.

Policy: Law No. 60 “On the basics of crime prevention.”
Policy_Content: This Law defines the legal and organizational framework for the prevention of offences and regulates public relations arising in the field of crime prevention in the Kyrgyz Republic. The goals of crime prevention shall be to increase the level of protection of citizens, a decrease in the level of crime, identification, elimination of the causes and conditions that contribute to committing offences. The tasks of crime prevention shall be as follows: (a) ensuring protection of rights, freedoms and legal interests of the individual; (b) raising the level of legal consciousness and legal culture of citizens and officials' responsibility, strengthening legality, as well as the formation of an intolerant attitude towards offences and violations of the law; (c) creation of systems for the prevention of offences and reorientation of state bodies from combating the consequences of crimes to the prevention of offences; (d) study and identification of the reasons for the commission of offences and conditions conducive to the commission of offences, acceptance of measures to eliminate them; (e) social rehabilitation and social adaptation of victims of offences,  prone to committing offences, as well as persons who have committed offences; and  (f) ensuring interaction of the subjects of prevention of offences by implementation of the prevention of offences. Prevention of offences shall be based on the following principles: (a) priority of human rights and freedoms, responsibility of subjects of the prevention of offences for ensuring human rights and freedoms; (b) legality; (c) ensuring the consistency and unity of approaches in the implementation of prevention of offenses; (c) openness, continuity, sequence, timeliness, objectivity, sufficiency and scientific substantiation of the measures taken to prevent offences; (d) competence and complexity in the implementation of prevention of offences; and (e) cooperation and interaction between subjects of prevention of offences. Special prevention of offences shall be intended the activity of subjects of crime prevention for the development and implementation of measures aimed at the prevention of certain types of offences, elimination of the reasons and conditions for their commission, identification of certain categories of persons and rendering them preventive assistance shall include combating corruption and prevention of crimes committed by officials.

Policy_Content: This Regional Law regulates certain issues in the field of manufacturing of organic products, and also determines the powers of the regional bodies of state power in the field of manufacturing of organic products. It does not apply to issues related to production, storage, transportation and sale of perfumery and cosmetics, medicines, seeds of forest plants, wildlife products and fish products (excluding aquaculture products). Organic producers shall be intended legal and physical persons who carry out production, storage, labelling, transportation and sale of organic products and are included in the unified state register of organic producers. The main directions of the regional state policy in the field of organic production are: (a) development of organic agriculture; (b) increasing the competitiveness of agricultural commodities, produced in the regional territory; (c) providing the population with high-quality and safe foodstuffs; and (d) state support for organic producers. In the transition to organic agriculture and organic production, a transitional period is established during which implementation of the rules of organic agriculture and organic production is ensured, as established by the national, interstate and international standards in the field of organic production acting in the Russian Federation. It is not allowed to place the label of organic products on packaging, consumer, transport packaging of agricultural commodities, raw materials and foodstuffs produced during the transition period.

Policy: Decreto Ley 135/021 - Reglamento de calidad del aire.
Policy_Content: El presente decreto ley adopta el Reglamento de calidad del aire como norma de referencia para dicha materia. El reglamento tiene por objetivo la protección del ambiente a través de la prevención de la contaminación del aire, mediante el establecimiento de objetivos de calidad de aire para disminuir los riesgos para la salud humana y los ecosistemas, y la fijación de límites máximos de emisión, tanto para fuentes fijas como móviles. Se establecen como objetivos de calidad del aire, los niveles máximos que para ciertos parámetros se pretenden alcanzar y mantener en el aire ambiente, según se presentan en la Tabla 1, aplicables desde la publicación de este reglamento y hasta el 31 de diciembre de 2023, y, en la Tabla 2, aplicables a partir del 1 ° de enero de 2024. Los objetivos de calidad del aire pautarán los planes, programas y actos que se desarrollen en torno a la evaluación, regulación, autorización y control de las fuentes de contaminación del aire en todo el territorio nacional.

Policy_Content: El presente documento, elaborado por el Ministerio de Planificación Nacional y Política Económica (Mideplan), está orientado a fortalecer los procesos de generación de bienes de capital. Este análisis permite incorporar, al momento de la evaluación de los proyectos, los costos asociados a las medidas de prevención y mitigación de estos riesgos para la continuidad del servicio durante su vida útil. La metodología que se presenta sirve como herramienta de referencia para que las entidades a cargo de la infraestructura pública puedan aplicarla para la evaluación del riesgo bajo un enfoque multiamenaza en todo el ciclo de vida de los proyectos de inversión pública, como lo establece el Artículo 5 del Decreto Ejecutivo 42465-MOPT-MINAE-MIVAH referente a los Lineamientos generales para la incorporación de las medidas de resiliencia en infraestructura pública.
